definition_zh: 考试；检查；审查；诊察；质证
definition_en: a formal test of knowledge, or a careful inspection of something
core_image: 天平中央那根指针：一边放砝码，一边放待称的东西，指针偏转就说明重量。
scene: 考场上，学生翻开试卷，计时器开始走动；同一周里，医生也在给另一位病人做检查。In the hall a student opens the paper as the timer starts, and that same week a doctor carries out an examination of another patient.
sceneCN: 这里 examination 同时体现「考试」和「医学检查」两个意思（考场用第 1 个义项，身体检查用第 3 个义项）；句意：考场里学生翻开试卷、计时器开始走动；同一周里，医生也在给另一位病人做检查。

senses.title: A formal test
senses.titleCN: 考试：用题目测知识或能力
senses.definition: a formal test of knowledge or ability, usually written or spoken
senses.definitionCN: 对知识或能力的正式测试，通常为笔试或口试
senses.example: The final examination covers everything from the first term.
senses.exampleCN: 期末考试覆盖第一学期以来的全部内容。
senses.why: A test is a weighing: the candidate's knowledge is placed against a fixed standard, and the mark records the difference.
senses.whyCN: 考试就是一次称重：考生的知识被放到固定标准旁，分数记录了两者的差距。

senses.title: Close inspection
senses.definition: a careful look at something in order to find out its condition or details
senses.definitionCN: 为查明状况或细节而仔细查看某物
senses.example: A close examination showed a hairline crack in the frame.
senses.exampleCN: 仔细检查发现框架上有一条细裂缝。
senses.why: The original image is a balance pointer: examination is the act of bringing something under scrutiny so that its hidden weight shows.
senses.whyCN: 原意象是天平的指针：examination 就是把东西放到审视之下，让隐藏的‘重量’显现。

senses.title: Medical examination
senses.titleCN: 医学检查：把身体放到诊断标准下
senses.definition: a physical or clinical check of a patient's body or health
senses.definitionCN: 对病人身体或健康状况进行的体格或临床检查
senses.example: The doctor began the examination with the patient's breathing.
senses.exampleCN: 医生从病人的呼吸开始检查。
senses.why: The body becomes the object weighed against normal signs; the examination looks for what departs from the expected range.
senses.whyCN: 身体成为对照正常体征被称量的对象；检查寻找的是偏离预期范围的部分。

senses.title: Cross-examination
senses.titleCN: 法律质证：用问题检验证词
senses.definition: the questioning of a witness by the opposing side in a legal case
senses.definitionCN: 法律案件中由对方对证人进行的提问与检验
senses.example: Cross-examination exposed a contradiction in the witness's account.
senses.exampleCN: 交叉质证暴露了证人陈述中的矛盾。
senses.why: A witness's story is put on the scale of other evidence; each question tests whether it still balances.
senses.whyCN: 证人的说法被放到其他证据的天平上；每个问题都在检验它是否仍然平衡。

senses.title: Official inquiry
senses.titleCN: 官方审查：对事件与账目立案调查
senses.definition: a formal investigation by an authority into an event or a set of records
senses.definitionCN: 权威机构对事件或记录进行的正式调查
senses.example: The committee's examination of the accounts lasted six months.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会对账目的审查持续了六个月。
senses.why: An authority sets the standard and compels the records to be produced; the examination is the forced comparison.
senses.whyCN: 权威设定标准并强制调取记录；examination 就是这场强制性的对照。

senses.title: Academic scrutiny
senses.titleCN: 学术审查：把论文与证据逐条核对
senses.definition: the critical review of a scholarly claim, text, or body of evidence
senses.definitionCN: 对学术主张、文本或证据体系进行的批判性审查
senses.example: The theory did not survive examination by later researchers.
senses.exampleCN: 该理论没能经受后来研究者的审查。
senses.why: In scholarship the balance is evidence: a claim is examined by asking whether the evidence outweighs the objections.
senses.whyCN: 学术里的天平是证据：审查一个主张，就是问证据是否压过反方意见。

senses.title: Laboratory test
senses.titleCN: 化验：把样本放到仪器里检验
senses.definition: a laboratory procedure that tests a sample for particular substances or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室检验样本中特定物质或状况的程序
senses.example: Examination of the water sample revealed high lead levels.
senses.exampleCN: 对水样的化验显示铅含量偏高。
senses.why: Here the instrument replaces the human eye; the sample is examined because its contents are not visible without a test.
senses.whyCN: 这里仪器替代了眼睛；样本之所以被检验，是因为不测试就看不见其中的成分。

senses.title: Testing a hypothesis
senses.definition: the process of testing a hypothesis, idea, or method against evidence
senses.definitionCN: 用证据对假设、观点或方法进行检验的过程
senses.example: The proposal came under examination during the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 该方案在试验期间受到了检验。
senses.why: An idea is examined by putting it in a situation where it could fail. Passing the examination is not proof, only survival so far.
senses.whyCN: 检验一个想法，就是把它放进可能失败的处境。通过检验不是证明，只是截至目前还活着。

intro.en: Examination comes from Latin examen, the tongue or pointer of a balance, and examinare, to weigh or test. The weighing image is older than the school sense.
intro.cn: examination 来自拉丁 examen（天平的指针）与 examinare（称量、检验）。‘称重’的意象比‘考试’义更古老。

items.en: The pointer or tongue of a balance, hence a means of weighing. The word names the instrument that reveals weight, not the weight itself.
items.cn: 天平的指针或舌，因而指称量的手段。这个词命名的是显示重量的器具，而不是重量本身。

items.en: To drive out, to demand, to weigh. Many sources connect examen with exigere, but the link is reconstructed rather than directly attested; it is best marked as generally accepted, not certain.
items.cn: 驱出、索取、称量。许多来源把 examen 与 exigere 联系起来，但这是重构而非直接可证的联系；宜标为“一般认为是”，不是确定结论。

items.en: To weigh, test, or examine. The verb extends the balance image to any careful assessment of a thing's value or truth.
items.cn: 称量、检验、审查。该动词把天平意象扩展到对事物价值或真实性的任何仔细评估。

items.en: Old French passed the noun to English. The French form kept both the legal and the scholarly possibilities of the Latin verb.
items.cn: 古法语把该名词传给英语。法语形式同时保留了拉丁动词的法律与学术两种可能。

items.en: English examination is recorded from the 14th century, first in legal and religious inquiry, then in academic testing.
items.cn: 英语 examination 自 14 世纪有记录，先用于法律与宗教调查，后用于学业测试。

items.en: The school examination became fixed in the 19c as public education expanded. Medicine and science kept the older sense of inspecting a body or a sample.
items.cn: 19 世纪公共教育扩张，学校‘考试’义固定下来；医学与科学则保留更古老的‘检查身体或样本’义。

note.en: The first group is the examine family; the second compares kinds of checking, from a scored test to a broad inquiry.
note.cn: 第一组是 examine 词族；第二组比较各种‘检查’，从计分考试到广泛调查。

entries.definition: to inspect or test something carefully. It is the action behind examination.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细检查或检验；是 examination 背后的动作。

entries.definition: a person who sets or marks an examination, or who inspects something officially.
entries.definitionCN: 出题或评卷的人，或进行官方检查的人。

entries.definition: a person who is being examined, especially in a test. The suffix -ee marks the receiver.
entries.definitionCN: 接受考试或检查的人；后缀 -ee 标记接受者。

entries.definition: the informal short form of examination in the school sense. It is not used for medical inspection.
entries.definitionCN: 学校义项中 examination 的非正式缩略；不用于医学检查。

entries.definition: a procedure that measures ability or quality, often with a score. It is the everyday word for a school examination.
entries.definitionCN: 测量能力或质量的程序，常带分数；是学校考试的日常用词。

entries.definition: an official or careful look at something to check its condition. It stresses seeing rather than questioning.
entries.definitionCN: 为核查状况而进行的官方或仔细查看；强调‘看’，而非‘问’。

entries.definition: a judgement of quality, ability, or risk. It is broader than a single examination.
entries.definitionCN: 对质量、能力或风险的判断；比单次考试更宽泛。

entries.definition: a formal or systematic investigation into a question. It emphasizes seeking facts, not grading.
entries.definitionCN: 对某个问题的正式或系统调查；强调寻找事实，而非评分。

entries.definition: a quick check to identify cases that need closer attention. It is an examination used as a filter.
entries.definitionCN: 为找出需要进一步关注的对象而做的快速检查；是作为筛选器的 examination。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin examen, the pointer of a balance, plus -ation. The word asks what something weighs when placed against a standard.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁 examen‘天平指针’加 -ation。这个词问的是：把某物放到标准旁，它有多重。

normal.en: A balance pointer is the original examination: it shows the hidden weight.
normal.cn: 天平指针就是最初的 examination：它让隐藏的重量显形。

normal.en: An exam paper is a balance: your answer on one side, the mark scheme on the other.
normal.cn: 试卷就是天平：一边你的答案，一边评分标准。

normal.en: A doctor's examination puts your body beside normal ranges.
normal.cn: 医生的 examination 把身体放到正常范围旁边。

normal.en: Cross-examination weighs one story against other evidence.
normal.cn: 交叉质证用其他证据来称量一个说法。

normal.en: A lab examination reveals what the eye cannot weigh.
normal.cn: 实验室检查揭示眼睛称不出来的东西。

abstract.en: To examine is to risk an answer, not to confirm one.
abstract.cn: 审查是让答案承担风险，而不是确认答案。

abstract.en: Every examination chooses its instrument, and the instrument decides what can be found.
abstract.cn: 每次检查都选择自己的仪器，而仪器决定了能发现什么。

abstract.en: A test measures the answer, not the person; the confusion between them is a social fact.
abstract.cn: 考试测量的是答案，不是人；把两者混为一谈是一种社会事实。

examples.en: The examination was moved online after the snow closed the school.
examples.cn: 大雪停课后，考试改到了线上。

examples.en: A second examination of the manuscript found a date written in a later hand.
examples.cn: 对抄本的再次检查发现了一个后来补写的日期。

examples.en: Under examination, the witness admitted he had not seen the car.
examples.cn: 在质证中，证人承认他并没有看见那辆车。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一个贼，没捏住”——考试时想作弊，被老师“捏住”检查：examination 检查、考试。

root: 源自拉丁 examen（天平指针）与 examinare（称量、检验），经古法语 examinacion 进入英语；核心是“把对象放到标准上称一称”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of examination, one gesture: place something against a standard and see how it weighs. The standard can be a mark scheme, a normal range, another witness, an authority's rule, a body of evidence, or an instrument.
sensesIntro.cn: examination 的八个义项共用一个动作：把对象放到标准上，看它有多重。标准可以是评分方案、正常范围、另一份证词、权威规则、证据体系或仪器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the pointer of a balance swinging as a weight is placed on one side.
core.cn: 核心意象：砝码放上一边时，天平指针摆动。

branches.en: TESTING CLAIMS: a school paper and a scholarly thesis are both weighed against a standard.
branches.cn: 检验主张：试卷与学术论文都被放到标准上称量。

branches.en: BRINGING TO LIGHT: close inspection and hypothesis testing reveal what was hidden.
branches.cn: 让隐者显形：仔细检查与假设检验都揭示隐藏的东西。

branches.en: READING THE BODY OR SAMPLE: the clinic and the laboratory use instruments to weigh what the eye cannot see.
branches.cn: 读取身体或样本：诊所与实验室用仪器称量眼睛看不见的东西。

branches.en: QUESTIONING A WITNESS: cross-examination weighs one account against other evidence.
branches.cn: 质询证人：交叉质证用一个说法对账其他证据。

branches.en: INVESTIGATING RECORDS: an authority compels documents into the open for comparison.
branches.cn: 调查记录：权威强制把文件摆出来做对照。

intro.en: Examination is examin- plus -ation. English also has the verb examine, the person nouns examiner and examinee, and the clipped form exam.
intro.cn: examination 是 examin- 加 -ation。英语还有动词 examine、人物名词 examiner 与 examinee，以及缩略形式 exam。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms are examen, examinare, and exigere. The connection between examen and exigere is generally accepted but reconstructed, so it should not be presented as certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁形式是 examen、examinare、exigere。examen 与 exigere 的联系被普遍接受，但属于重构，不应说成确定事实。

items.example: The panel examined every page of the report.
items.exampleCN: 专家组审查了报告的每一页。

items.example: The examiner checked the seal on each sample.
items.exampleCN: 审查员检查了每个样本上的封条。

items.example: Each examinee received a numbered desk.
items.exampleCN: 每位应试者拿到一张编号课桌。

items.example: She has three exams next week.

items.meaning: to question a witness for the opposing side
items.example: The lawyer cross-examined the witness for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 律师盘问证人一个小时。

items.meaning: the questioning of a witness by the other side
items.example: Cross-examination is limited to the scope of direct testimony.
items.exampleCN: 交叉质证限于直接证词的范围。

items.meaning: precise, or to demand and obtain
items.meaningCN: 精确的；强求；源自 exigere‘驱出、索取’
items.example: The exact wording of the clause matters.
items.exampleCN: 该条款的精确措辞很重要。

items.meaningCN: 紧急的；迫切需要处理的
items.example: The exigent circumstances justified a late-night call.
items.exampleCN: 紧急情况使得深夜致电成为正当。

items.example: The budget was cut in response to a fiscal exigency.
items.exampleCN: 为应对财政紧急状况，预算被削减。

latinEntries.meaning: the tongue or pointer of a balance; a weighing

latinEntries.meaningCN: 驱出；索取；称量（与 examen 的联系属一般认为）

definition_en: to look at something closely and in detail in order to judge its condition, quality or truth
core_image: 一架老式天平，指针停在刻度之间，旁边放着待称的信封与放大镜
scene: 一位技师把送来的旧钟拆开，逐枚查看齿轮的磨损痕迹。A conservator examines each gear under a magnifier before ordering repairs.
sceneCN: 技师拆开旧钟，逐枚查看齿轮磨损；句中的 examine 指「仔细查看以判断状况」（第 1 个义项：近距离细看以了解状态）。图中可辨识物件：拆开的机芯、放大镜、镊子、记录纸。

senses.title: Look closely at a thing
senses.titleCN: 近距离细看以判断状况
senses.definition: to inspect something closely in order to learn its condition
senses.definitionCN: 近距离查看某物，以了解其状况
senses.example: A conservator examines each gear under a magnifier.
senses.exampleCN: 修复师在放大镜下逐枚检查齿轮。
senses.why: the Latin verb came from the noun for the tongue of a balance, so the earliest picture is a needle settling to show how much something weighs.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词来自表示「天平指针」的名词，因此最早的意象是一根指针停稳，显示某物有多重。

senses.title: Test a student's knowledge
senses.definition: to question a student in order to measure what has been learned
senses.definitionCN: 通过提问来测量学生学到了什么
senses.example: The committee examines candidates in both written and oral rounds.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会用笔试与口试两轮考查候选人。
senses.why: a balance decides value by an exact measure, and an examiner does the same with a candidate's knowledge, which is why the school sense came early.
senses.whyCN: 天平用精确的衡量判定价值，主考人对考生的知识做的也是同一件事，因此学校义很早就出现了。

senses.title: Investigate formally
senses.definition: to go through evidence in an official inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 在正式调查中逐项查验证据
senses.example: Lawyers examined the invoices line by line.
senses.exampleCN: 律师逐行审查了这些发票。
senses.why: the weighing image fits legal inquiry: each item is placed on the scale and its weight argued.
senses.whyCN: 称量的意象正合法律调查：每一件证据都被放上天平，再争论它的分量。

senses.title: Check a patient
senses.definition: to inspect a person's body to find signs of illness
senses.definitionCN: 查看人体以发现疾病的迹象
senses.example: The doctor examined the ankle and sent him for a scan.
senses.exampleCN: 医生检查了脚踝，又让他去做扫描。
senses.why: the medical sense is the general inspection sense narrowed to the body, where signs must be found before a judgement is made.
senses.whyCN: 医学义是把一般查看收窄到身体：必须先找到迹象，才能作出判断。

senses.title: Analyse data critically
senses.definition: to study information closely to find patterns or errors
senses.definitionCN: 细究信息以找出规律或错误
senses.example: The team examined the readings for seasonal drift.
senses.exampleCN: 团队细查读数，寻找季节性漂移。
senses.why: data has to be weighed in the same way as goods: the verb keeps its old sense of testing rather than merely seeing.
senses.whyCN: 数据也要像货物一样被称量：这个动词保留的是「检验」而非「看见」的旧义。

senses.title: Question a witness
senses.definition: to question a witness formally, especially in court
senses.definitionCN: 正式询问证人，尤指在法庭上
senses.example: The defence examined the witness for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方盘问证人达两小时。
senses.why: courtroom question and balance share an origin: both force an account to show its weight under pressure.
senses.whyCN: 法庭讯问与天平同源：二者都迫使一份陈述在压力下显出分量。

senses.title: Inspect goods
senses.definition: to check goods for quality or damage before accepting them
senses.definitionCN: 在接受货物前查看其质量或损坏情况
senses.example: The buyer examined the crates before signing.
senses.exampleCN: 买方在签字前检验了木箱。
senses.why: trade kept the most literal sense, because a merchant must look at what is being weighed and paid for.
senses.whyCN: 商贸保留了最字面的意义，因为商人必须看清被称量、被付钱的东西。

senses.title: Weigh a proposal
senses.definition: to consider an idea carefully before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在作决定前仔细考虑一个想法
senses.example: The board examined every option before voting.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会在投票前审议了每一个选项。
senses.why: the balance image turns abstract: options are placed one after another on the same scale until a choice settles.
senses.whyCN: 天平的意象在此抽象化：选项被逐一放上同一架秤，直到选择落定。

intro.en: Examine comes from Latin examinare 'to weigh, test', built on examen, the noun for the tongue or needle of a balance, which itself goes back to exigere 'to drive out, to weigh'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: examine 来自拉丁 examinare「称量、检验」，其名词 examen 指天平的指针或舌杆，而 examen 又可追溯至 exigere「驱出、称量」。年代为约数。

items.en: Exigere combined ex- 'out' with agere 'to drive, do' and meant 'to drive out, to demand, to weigh exactly'. The weighing sense grew from the demand for exact measure.
items.cn: exigere 由 ex-「出」与 agere「驱使、做」构成，意为「驱出、索求、精确称量」。称量义由对精确衡量的要求发展而来。

items.en: Examen named the tongue of a balance, the pointer that settles when the two pans hold equal weight.
items.cn: examen 指天平的舌杆，即两盘等重时停稳的那根指针。

items.en: From the noun came examinare 'to weigh, to test, to inquire into', used for both goods and arguments.
items.cn: 由这个名词产生 examinare「称量、检验、查究」，既用于货物也用于论辩。

items.en: Old French examiner carried the verb into English in the fourteenth century, first in the legal and scholarly senses.
items.cn: 古法语 examiner 在十四世纪把这个动词带入英语，最初用于法律与学术场合。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the verb covered questioning a candidate and inspecting a patient, both extensions of testing.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个动词已涵盖考查考生与检查病人，二者都是「检验」的延伸。

items.en: The detail that examen meant specifically the balance tongue is generally accepted, but the deeper origin of agere and the exact route from exigere to examen are not fully settled; forms offered for a pre-Latin root are reconstructions.
items.cn: examen 特指天平舌杆这一细节一般认为是可靠的，但 agere 的更早来源以及从 exigere 到 examen 的确切路径尚无定论；为其拉丁语之前词根给出的形式属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the derived family and two words that merely look similar but come from a different verb; group two holds verbs of looking and testing that differ in pressure and purpose.
note.cn: 第一组是派生词族，以及两个只是形似、其实出自另一动词的词；第二组是查看与检验类动词，压力与目的各不相同。

entries.definition: The act or result of examining, and also the paper sat in a school; it cannot stand where the verb is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 检查或审查的行为与结果，也指学校里的试卷；不能代替动词。

entries.definition: The one who questions or inspects, not the act itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指提问或检查的人，而非行为本身。

entries.definition: Looks close but comes from eximere 'to take out', not from examen; an example is something taken out for display.
entries.definitionCN: 形近但出自 eximere「取出」，与 examen 无关；example 是被取出展示的样本。

entries.definition: Also from eximere: to take someone out of an obligation, with no notion of weighing.
entries.definitionCN: 同样出自 eximere：把某人从义务中取出，不含称量之意。

entries.definition: A formal look, often by an authority checking standards; examine is broader and can include testing.
entries.definitionCN: 正式查看，常指权威方查标准；examine 范围更广，可含检验。

entries.definition: To look into a matter over time, following leads; it stresses process more than the single act of weighing.
entries.definitionCN: 指沿线索在一段时间里查办某事，更强调过程而非单次称量。

entries.definition: To examine with suspicion and great closeness, adding doubt that examine does not carry.
entries.definitionCN: 带着怀疑极仔细地查看，多出 examine 所无的疑虑。

entries.definition: To make something show its quality by use or trial; examine may only look and judge.
entries.definitionCN: 通过使用或试用让某物显出品质；examine 可能只是查看并判断。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here are the real balance image, the real Latin steps, the real family and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自真实的天平意象、真实的拉丁演变、真实词族与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: examen was the tongue of a balance: to examine is to put something on the scale.
normal.cn: examen 是天平的舌杆：examine 就是把某物放上秤。

normal.en: ex- 'out' plus agere 'drive': to drive a matter out into the open where it can be weighed.
normal.cn: ex-「出」加 agere「驱使」：把一件事驱到明处，好称它的分量。

normal.en: The family runs examination, examiner, examinee, exam, cross-examine.
normal.cn: 词族包括 examination、examiner、examinee、exam、cross-examine。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: examine evidence, examine a patient, examine a witness.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出场景：审查证据、检查病人、询问证人。

normal.en: The passive is common in reports: the findings were examined by two reviewers.
normal.cn: 报告中常用被动式：研究结果由两位审稿人审查。

abstract.en: Picture a needle that will not settle until every doubt has been placed on one pan or the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一根指针，直到所有疑问都被放上这盘或那盘才肯停稳。

abstract.en: Picture a jeweller's loupe left on a tray of loose stones, each one already weighed.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚珠宝放大镜搁在一盘散石上，每颗都已称过。

abstract.en: Picture a courtroom where a sentence is literally hung on the scales.
abstract.cn: 想象一间法庭，判决就悬在天平上。

examples.en: The panel examined the proposal for hidden costs.
examples.cn: 小组审议了提案，寻找隐藏成本。

examples.en: She examined the transcript against the recording.
examples.cn: 她对照录音检查了文字稿。

examples.en: The vet examined the horse before the sale.
examples.cn: 兽医在售前检查了这匹马。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）+ amine（像「阿门」）」——把东西拿出来放到天平上称一称 → 检查、审查、考查

root: 拉丁 exigere「驱出、称量」→ 名词 examen「天平指针」→ 动词 examinare「称量、检验」→ 古法语 examiner → 英语 examine；agere 的更深来源与 exigere 到 examen 的确切路径尚无定论，相关词根形式属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses hang on one instrument: something is placed on a balance, and the same gesture is then used on a clock, a student, a file of evidence, an ankle, a data set, a witness, a crate and finally on a list of options.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项挂在同一件器具上：把某物放上天平，同一个动作随后用于旧钟、学生、证据卷宗、脚踝、数据集、证人、木箱，最后用于一列选项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance needle that only settles after everything has been put on the pans.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根天平指针，非等一切都被放上秤盘不肯停稳。

branches.en: PHYSICAL CHECK: a gear and a crate are both looked over before a judgement is passed.
branches.cn: 实物查验：齿轮与木箱都要先被看过，才有判断。

branches.en: QUESTIONING: a candidate and a witness are pressed to show what they carry.
branches.cn: 盘问：考生与证人都被追问，要他们显出分量。

branches.en: PAPER AND NUMBERS: invoices and readings must be gone through line by line.
branches.cn: 纸面与数字：发票与读数都得逐行过一遍。

branches.en: BODY: the same inspection narrows to signs of illness in a patient.
branches.cn: 身体：同样的查看收窄为病人身上的疾病迹象。

branches.en: CHOICE: options are weighed one after another until the needle settles.
branches.cn: 抉择：选项被逐一称量，直到指针停稳。

intro.en: The verb is a Latin prefix and root plus two suffixes, and the same pieces build the whole examining family.
intro.cn: 这个动词由拉丁前缀、词根再加两个后缀构成，同一批部件也造出整个「检查」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin exigere and examen supply the core; the English suffixes -ation, -er and -ee build the nouns.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 exigere 与 examen 提供核心；英语中的名词后缀与表人后缀造出各个名词。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作向外驱出。

items.exampleCN: 这场审查持续了三小时。

items.example: The examiner read the answers twice.
items.exampleCN: 主考人把答案读了两遍。

items.example: Each examinee received a numbered seat.
items.exampleCN: 每位应试者都拿到一个编号座位。

items.example: The exam was moved to Friday.

items.meaning: to question a witness for the other side
items.meaningCN: 对另一方证人进行交叉询问
items.exampleCN: 律师交叉询问了那名职员。

definition_zh: 例子；实例；榜样；范例；样板
definition_en: a thing or person that is typical of a group, or a model that shows how something should be done
core_image: 货架上的样品：拿一个具体的东西放在你眼前，让你看清整类东西的样子
scene: 老师讲到几何题，班上没人听懂，她只好在黑板上画了一个三角形，边写边说：Let me give you an example so you can see how the rule works.
sceneCN: 这里 example 指「用来演示规则的例子」（第 1 个义项：说明某类事物的具体实例）；句意为老师举一个三角形的例子帮学生看懂规则。

derivatives.zh: 举例说明；是…的典型（example 加动词后缀 -ify，义为「拿例子来证明」）
可作楷模的；典范的（example 加形容词后缀 -ary，义为「堪称榜样的」）
模范；典型样本（拉丁词形直入英语，义为「被拿出来当样本的东西」）

senses.title: A concrete instance of a group or rule
senses.titleCN: 说明某类事物的具体实例
senses.definition: one particular thing that is taken from a group to show what the whole group is like
senses.definitionCN: 从一群同类事物中拿出一个具体的东西，用来展示这一整类的样子
senses.example: Let me give you an example so you can see how the rule works.
senses.exampleCN: 我举一个例子，好让你看懂这条规则怎么用。
senses.why: The core image is a sample on display: you cannot see an abstract rule directly, so you hold up one concrete case and let it stand for the whole.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是货架上的样品：抽象规则看不见，只能拿出一个具体案例，让它替整类东西说话。

senses.title: A person worthy of imitation
senses.definition: a person or behaviour that other people should try to copy because it is good
senses.definitionCN: 因为做得好而值得别人学着做的人或行为
senses.example: A good captain sets an example for the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 一个好队长会给全队树立榜样。
senses.why: When the sample is a person, the case on display is not just descriptive but prescriptive: others are expected to copy it.
senses.whyCN: 当「样品」换成人，摆出来的案例就不只是描述，还带上了要求：别人应该照着做。

senses.title: A warning instance
senses.definition: an instance of bad behaviour or failure that shows others what to avoid
senses.definitionCN: 用一件坏事或一次失败给旁人看，提醒他们别重蹈覆辙
senses.example: The judge made the punishment an example to future offenders.
senses.exampleCN: 法官重罚这名犯人，让后来的人引以为戒。
senses.why: A displayed case can point two ways: it can show what to copy, or what to avoid; the direction comes from context.
senses.whyCN: 摆出来的案例有两个指向：既可以是让人学的好样子，也可以是让人躲的坏下场；方向由语境决定。

senses.title: A problem to be solved as practice
senses.definition: a question or problem worked out as a model for learners to follow
senses.definitionCN: 把一道题完整解出来，给学习者照着做的一道示范题
senses.example: The textbook shows a worked example before each exercise set.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书在每组练习前都给出例题的完整解法。
senses.why: In teaching, the sample case is a solved problem: the learner first watches the rule in action, then repeats it alone.
senses.whyCN: 在教学里，样品就是解好的一道题：学习者先看规则运行一遍，再自己重复一遍。

senses.title: A typical representative of a kind
senses.definition: a thing that fairly represents the typical qualities of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 能公平代表某一类东西典型特征的物件
senses.example: This old machine is a fine example of early engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧机器是早期工程技术的优秀代表。
senses.why: The sample stands for the whole group only if it is typical; so an example also carries the meaning of a fair representative.
senses.whyCN: 样品要能代表全体，前提是它够典型；所以 example 也带上「典型代表」的意思。

intro.en: Example runs straight back to Latin, through French, and its root image is "taking something out" to be seen.
intro.cn: example 一路源自拉丁语、经古法语进入英语，词根画面是「把某样东西拿出来」给人看。

items.en: Latin exemplum meant "a sample, a pattern, a warning case", from eximere "to take out", built on ex- (out) + emere (to take).
items.cn: 拉丁语 exemplum 意为「样品、范例、警示案例」，来自 eximere「取出」，由 ex-（向外）+ emere（拿）构成。

items.en: The underlying image is literally taking one item out of a pile so that it can be examined as a stand-in for the rest.
items.cn: 底层画面就是从一堆东西里拿出一件，让它充当其余物品的代表接受检视。

items.en: Old French carried the word as essample / example, keeping the sense of model and warning.
items.cn: 古法语以 essample / example 的形式继承了这个词，保留了「模范」「警示」的意思。

items.en: Middle English borrowed it from French as example by the thirteenth century, covering both instance and model.
items.cn: 十三世纪中古英语从法语借入 example，同时覆盖「实例」与「典范」两义。

items.en: Modern English kept both lines: a neutral instance to clarify, and a model to imitate or a warning to avoid.
items.cn: 现代英语保留两条线：用来讲清楚的中性实例，以及供效仿的模范或供引以为戒的警示。

note.en: The words below are close to example in spelling or in the idea of a displayed case.
note.cn: 下面的词在拼写上或「摆出案例给人看」这层意思上与 example 相近。

entries.definition: a model or ideal pattern worth copying
entries.definitionCN: 模范；理想范式（与 example 同根，拉丁词形直接入英语）

entries.definition: serving as a desirable model; very good
entries.definitionCN: 堪称典范的（同根形容词）

entries.definition: free from an obligation or duty required of others
entries.definitionCN: 被免除的（拼写相近但词根不同，来自 exonera 一族，义为「免除」）

entries.definition: a small part taken to show what the whole is like
entries.definitionCN: 样品；样本（与 example 同源于拉丁 eximere）

entries.definition: a single case of something happening
entries.definitionCN: 一个具体事例（强调事件性的一次）

entries.definition: a standard thing to copy
entries.definitionCN: 典范；模型（强调「值得照着做」）

entries.definition: an example that makes a point clearer
entries.definitionCN: 说明性实例（为讲清观点而举）

normalIntro.en: Five steady associations built from the real word family and collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实词族与搭配的稳当联想。

normal.en: ex- means out, so an example is a case taken out of the group for display.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex- 表示「向外」，example 就是「从一堆里拿出来展示」的那一件。

normal.en: Give an example: teachers hold up one triangle to stand for all triangles.
normal.cn: 举例子：老师举一个三角形，让它代表所有三角形。

normal.en: Set an example: a good captain is also a displayed sample of behaviour.
normal.cn: 树立榜样：好队长本身就是被摆出来的「行为样品」。

normal.en: Exemplify is the verb twin: one clear case exemplifies the rule.
normal.cn: exemplify 是动词孪生词：一个清楚的案例就能证明规则。

normal.en: For example is the everyday hinge that opens any clarification.
normal.cn: for example 是日常口头禅，一说出口就开始举例讲清楚。

abstract.en: Picture a shop shelf: one item is pulled forward under a spotlight as the sample.
abstract.cn: 想象一个货架：一件商品被拉到聚光灯下当样品。

abstract.en: The spotlight case can shine as a hero to copy or as a warning to avoid.
abstract.cn: 聚光灯下的案例可以是供效仿的英雄，也可以是供引以为戒的反面教材。

abstract.en: An abstract rule has no face until one example gives it a body.
abstract.cn: 抽象规则原本没有面孔，直到一个例子给它安上血肉。

examples.en: Let me give you an example so you can see how the rule works.
examples.cn: 我举一个例子，好让你看懂这条规则怎么用。

examples.en: A good captain sets an example for the whole team.
examples.cn: 一个好队长会给全队树立榜样。

examples.en: This old machine is a fine example of early engineering.
examples.cn: 这台旧机器是早期工程技术的优秀代表。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一个赞助普」——有人赞助了一件普通样品，把它摆在最显眼的位置当例子。

root: 源自拉丁语 exemplum「样品、范例」，来自动词 eximere「取出」，由 ex-（向外）+ emere（拿、取）构成；一般认为 emere 在此取「拿到手」义。经古法语 essample 进入中古英语后拼成 example。

sensesIntro.en: From a concrete case held up for inspection, the word widens into models to copy and warning cases to avoid.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个被拿出来检视的具体案例，扩展到供效仿的典范与供引以为戒的警示案例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one case pulled out of the group and put on display
core.cn: 核心意象：从一堆同类中拉出一件，摆出来给人看

branches.en: the displayed case clarifies a rule
branches.cn: 摆出来的案例把规则讲清楚

branches.en: the case becomes a model to imitate
branches.cn: 案例变成供效仿的典范

branches.en: the case becomes a warning to avoid
branches.cn: 案例变成供引以为戒的警示

branches.en: the case fairly stands for its kind
branches.cn: 案例公平地代表它的类别

branches.en: sampling logic: one part speaks for the whole
branches.cn: 取样逻辑：以部分代言整体

intro.en: The example family is small but regular, all built on the Latin root em- (take) with ex- (out).
intro.cn: example 词族不大但规律清晰，全部建立在拉丁词根 em-（拿取）加 ex-（向外）之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin cousins that keep the "take out" root.
latinIntro.cn: 保留「取出」词根的拉丁同族词。

items.meaningCN: 在此词族中表「取出来充作」（exemplum 中）
免除（拼写相近，词根另一支）

items.meaning: to put a case on display as a model
the Latin form kept in English

definition_zh: 极好的；卓越的；优秀的；出色的
definition_en: extremely good; outstanding in quality
core_image: 高出众人一头的那个人：在一排人里，他被拔得最高、看得最清
scene: 运动会上全班都在跳高，杆子一次次升高，最后只剩他轻松越过最高一格，看台上传来喊声：That was an excellent jump!
sceneCN: 这里 excellent 指「质量上乘、高出一般」（第 1 个义项：品质极佳的）；句意为那一跳非常出色。

derivatives.zh: 卓越；优点（excellent 的名词形式，义为「高出常格的品德或品质」）
超过；胜过（同源，义为「越过边界」）
胜过；擅长（同根动词，义为「高出他人」）

senses.title: Of outstanding quality
senses.definition: extremely good in quality or standard
senses.definitionCN: 质量或水准非常高
senses.example: That was an excellent jump!
senses.exampleCN: 那一跳跳得非常出色！
senses.why: The root image is being lifted above the line: what is excellent stands higher than the ordinary grade around it.
senses.whyCN: 词根画面是「被抬到线以上」：excellent 的东西比周围普通水准高出一截。

senses.title: Showing great skill or ability
senses.definition: showing a very high level of skill or ability
senses.definitionCN: 技艺或能力达到很高的水平
senses.example: She is excellent at explaining difficult ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 她特别擅长把难懂的想法讲明白。
senses.why: Being above the line in performance, not just in material quality, extends the image to people and their skills.
senses.whyCN: 「高出线」不只是东西的质量，也可以落在人的表现上，于是延伸到技艺层面。

senses.title: Used as strong approval
senses.definition: used to show strong approval or agreement, often as a single word
senses.definitionCN: 常以单词形式单独喊出，表示强烈赞同
senses.example: Excellent! We will go with your plan.
senses.exampleCN: 太好了！就按你的方案办。
senses.why: When the judgment is spoken alone, the comparative image stays but the sentence shrinks to pure praise.
senses.whyCN: 判断被单独喊出时，「高出一线」的画面还在，句子却缩成纯粹的赞许。

senses.title: Of very good health or condition
senses.definition: in very good health or physical condition
senses.definitionCN: 身体或物品处于很好的状态
senses.example: The old car is in excellent condition.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧车车况极佳。
senses.why: The line being compared against is the expected state; staying well above it is still the same image of being raised up.
senses.whyCN: 比较线是预期状态，状态远高于预期，仍是「被抬高」这一意象。

intro.en: Excellent climbs out of Latin via French, and its root means literally "to rise high, to outdo".
intro.cn: excellent 经法语源自拉丁语，词根本义是「升高、超出」。

items.en: Latin excellere meant "to rise up, to be eminent", from ex- (out, up) + a base -cellere related to celsus "high".
items.cn: 拉丁语 excellere 意为「升高、出众」，由 ex-（向上、向外）加词干构成，词干与 celsus「高」同源。

items.en: The picture is of something being lifted above a surrounding level, which is why the word always implies comparison.
items.cn: 画面是某物被抬到周围水准之上，因此这个词天生含比较意味。

items.en: Old French carried it as excellent, an adjective already in learned use.
items.cn: 古法语以 excellent 的形式继承，当时已是书面语形容词。

items.en: Middle English took it from French in the fourteenth century, first meaning "surpassing, excelling".
items.cn: 十四世纪中古英语从法语借入，最初义为「胜过、超越」。

items.en: Modern English settled it as the everyday top grade of praise, from objects to skills to bare exclamations.
items.cn: 现代英语把它定为日常赞美的最高档，从物品、技艺到单独的感叹都在用。

note.en: Nearby words share the spelling family or the idea of standing above the ordinary.
note.cn: 相邻的词与 excellent 同族，或同样有「高出寻常」的意思。

entries.definition: to be very good at something
entries.definitionCN: 擅长；胜过（同根动词）

entries.definition: the quality of being outstanding
entries.definitionCN: 卓越；优点（同根名词）

entries.definition: to go beyond a limit or number
entries.definitionCN: 超过（同源，义为「越界」）

entries.definition: not including; but not
entries.definitionCN: 除了（拼写相近但词根不同，来自 capere「抓取」一族）

entries.definition: clearly much better than others
entries.definitionCN: 杰出的（同样有「站在人群之外」的画面）

entries.definition: of the highest quality
entries.definitionCN: 极好的；华丽的

entries.definition: impressively good
entries.definitionCN: 极好的；辉煌的

normalIntro.en: Five associations grounded in the real root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 五条建立在真实词根与词族上的联想。

normal.en: ex- (up/out) + cell- (high): something raised above the line.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex-（向上）+ 词根 cell-（高）：某物被抬到线以上。

normal.en: Excel is the verb: he excels at maths, so his work is excellent.
normal.cn: excel 是动词：他数学出众，所以他的作业 excellent。

normal.en: Excellence is the noun: the school prizes academic excellence.
normal.cn: excellence 是名词：学校重视学术卓越。

normal.en: Exceed shares the rising image: the result exceeds all hopes.
normal.cn: exceed 共享「升高」的画面：结果超出所有期望。

normal.en: Shouting "Excellent!" is giving the top grade out loud.
normal.cn: 喊一声 "Excellent!" 就是大声打出最高分。

abstract.en: Picture a bar being raised in a high-jump contest until one jumper clears it easily.
abstract.cn: 想象跳高比赛的横杆不断升高，最后只剩一人轻松越过。

abstract.en: Everything ordinary sits under the line; the excellent thing stands above it in clear air.
abstract.cn: 平常的东西都在线以下，卓越的东西立在清朗的高处。

abstract.en: Praise is a ranking act: to call something excellent is to lift it in words.
abstract.cn: 称赞是一种排名：说某物 excellent，就是用语言把它抬高。

examples.en: That was an excellent jump!
examples.cn: 那一跳跳得非常出色！

examples.en: She is excellent at explaining difficult ideas.
examples.cn: 她特别擅长把难懂的想法讲明白。

examples.en: The old car is in excellent condition.
examples.cn: 这辆旧车车况极佳。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱克塞乐」——爱到可以塞满快乐，因为好得不得了，简直「爱克塞乐」。

root: 源自拉丁语 excellere「升高、出众」，由 ex-（向上、向外）+ 词干 -cellere 构成，词干与 celsus「高」同源；一般认为原义与「被抬高」的画面相关。经古法语进入中古英语。

sensesIntro.en: From being raised above the ordinary line, the word spreads to skills, condition, and bare spoken praise.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「高出寻常一线」出发，扩展到技艺、状态乃至脱口而出的赞许。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: lifted above the common line
core.cn: 核心意象：被抬到众人所在的普通线以上

branches.en: quality or condition above the norm
branches.cn: 质量或状态超出常规

branches.en: skill raised above the crowd
branches.cn: 技艺高出一众

branches.en: praise spoken as a single lifted word
branches.cn: 赞许单独成词喊出

branches.en: excelling implies comparison
branches.cn: 卓越天生含比较

branches.en: high performance earns admiration
branches.cn: 高表现赢得赞许

intro.en: The family keeps the Latin ex- (up, out) plus the high-root, with regular English suffixes.
intro.cn: 词族保留拉丁 ex-（向上）与「高」词根，再接规则英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin cousins that carry the rising root.
latinIntro.cn: 带「升高」词根的拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 除…之外；除了；要不是；只是
definition_en: not including; used before a statement that forms an exception to what has just been said
core_image: 从一把抓起的东西里松开一只手：大家都在里面，只有它被放出去
scene: 全家出游的合影人人都在笑，只有被留下看家的狗趴在门口，主人叹了口气说：Everyone went to the park except the dog.
sceneCN: 这里 except 指「把某物排除在外」（第 1 个义项：不包含在所谈范围之内）；句意为大家都去了公园，只有狗没去。

derivatives.zh: 例外（except 加名词后缀 -ion，义为「被拿出去的那一件」）
例外的；杰出的（exception 加形容词后缀，义为「作为例外的，进而指超出常格的」）
接受；收下（拼写相近的近亲词，义为「收进来」）

senses.title: Not included in a statement
senses.titleCN: 不包含在所谈范围之内
senses.definition: used before naming the one person or thing that is left out of a general statement
senses.definitionCN: 用在一般性说法之前，点出被排除在外的那个人或物
senses.example: Everyone went to the park except the dog.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都去了公园，只有狗没去。
senses.why: The root image is grabbing with the hand: from everything taken in, one item is caught and lifted out.
senses.whyCN: 词根画面是用手抓取：在全部纳入的东西里，有一件被单独拎了出来。

senses.title: Apart from the mentioned fact
senses.definition: used to add the one fact that is different from what has been said
senses.definitionCN: 补充与前面说法不同的一点
senses.example: I would join you except that I have homework.
senses.exampleCN: 我本想跟你去，只是我有作业。
senses.why: When the excluded item is a whole clause, the hand keeps holding everything but this one part of reality.
senses.whyCN: 当被排除的对象是一整句话时，那只手仍然抓着一切，只是松开现实中这一块。

senses.title: Only; nothing but
senses.definition: used after nothing, all, or only to say what remains
senses.definitionCN: 用在 nothing、all、only 之后，表示仅剩的内容
senses.example: There was nothing in the box except old letters.
senses.exampleCN: 盒子里除了几封旧信什么都没有。
senses.why: Reversing the view: instead of naming what leaves, the sentence names the single thing that stays inside the hand.
senses.whyCN: 换个视角：不说谁出去了，而说手里留下的仅有那一件事物。

senses.title: To leave out deliberately (formal verb)
senses.definition: to leave out or exclude from a general statement or rule
senses.definitionCN: 把某人某物从一般陈述或规则中排除
senses.example: The rule excepts members of the royal family.
senses.exampleCN: 该条款把王室成员排除在外。
senses.why: The verb keeps the literal hand-action: the rule itself reaches out and sets the item aside.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了字面上的手部动作：规则本身伸手把这一项挪开。

intro.en: Except grows from a Latin verb about seizing and taking out, through French, into a word about exclusion.
intro.cn: except 由拉丁语「抓住、取出」义的动词经法语演变而来，最终成为表示排除的词。

items.en: Latin excipere meant "to take out, to except", from ex- (out) + capere (to take, to seize).
items.cn: 拉丁语 excipere 意为「取出、排除」，由 ex-（向外）+ capere（拿、抓住）构成。

items.en: In legal Latin, excipere meant to single out a case so it fell outside a rule; this legal flavour stayed with the word.
items.cn: 在法律拉丁语里，excipere 指把一个情形单独拎出、使之不落入规则，法律色彩随之保留下来。

items.en: Old French took it as excepter, keeping the senses of removing and objecting.
items.cn: 古法语作 excepter，保留「移除」「提出异议」两义。

items.en: Middle English borrowed excepter in the fourteenth century as a verb and preposition together.
items.cn: 十四世纪中古英语借入 excepter，动词与介词用法同时进入。

items.en: Modern English kept the preposition except and the conjunction except that, while the verb except survived mostly in legal prose.
items.cn: 现代英语保留介词 except 与连词 except that，动词 except 主要存于法律文体。

note.en: Except is easy to confuse with its sibling accept, and sits near other excluding words.
note.cn: except 极易与同源的 accept 混淆，也与另几个排除类词相邻。

entries.definition: to take what is offered willingly
entries.definitionCN: 接受（前缀不同：ac- 向内收，except 是向外拿）

entries.definition: to think something will happen
entries.definitionCN: 预料；期待（拼写相近，词根为 spectare「看」）

entries.definition: a case that does not follow the rule
entries.definitionCN: 例外（同根名词）

entries.definition: a passage taken out of a text
entries.definitionCN: 摘录；节选（同根，取「抽出」义）

entries.definition: in addition to; apart from
entries.definitionCN: 除…之外（还有）；加上的口吻与 except 相反

entries.definition: not counting
entries.definitionCN: 不包括（正式书面）

entries.definition: except for; in addition to
entries.definitionCN: 除…之外（口语常用，方向视语境而定）

normalIntro.en: Five associations from the real root family and usage patterns.
normalIntro.cn: 五条来自真实词根词族与用法的联想。

normal.en: ex- (out) + cept (take): one thing is taken out of the group.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex-（向外）+ 词根 cept（拿）：有一件东西从整体里被拿出去。

normal.en: Exception is the noun: being late is the exception, not the rule.
normal.cn: exception 是名词：迟到是例外，不是常规。

normal.en: Accept points inward (receive), except points outward (exclude) — ac- versus ex-.
normal.cn: accept 向内（收下），except 向外（排除）——区别就在 ac- 与 ex-。

normal.en: Except for is the handy preposition: the essay is good except for one spelling.
normal.cn: except for 是顺手的介词：这篇作文很好，只是有一个拼写错误。

normal.en: Except that opens a whole clause: fine, except that it rains tomorrow.
normal.cn: except that 引导整句：都挺好，只是明天下雨。

abstract.en: Picture a handful of marbles: the fingers open and one marble drops out.
abstract.cn: 想象一把抓着弹珠的手：手指松开，一颗弹珠掉了出去。

abstract.en: The general statement is the closed hand; except is the moment of release.
abstract.cn: 一般性陈述是合拢的手，except 就是松手的那一下。

abstract.en: Exceptions draw boundaries: a rule only shows its edge where except cuts it.
abstract.cn: 例外画出边界：规则正是在 except 切开的地方露出边缘。

examples.en: Everyone went to the park except the dog.
examples.cn: 大家都去了公园，只有狗没去。

examples.en: I would join you except that I have homework.
examples.cn: 我本想跟你去，只是我有作业。

examples.en: There was nothing in the box except old letters.
examples.cn: 盒子里除了几封旧信什么都没有。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一颗塞普特」——一颗珠子被塞出来另放一边，剩下的都是「除…之外」。

root: 源自拉丁语 excipere「取出、排除」，由 ex-（向外）+ capere（拿、抓住）构成；法律拉丁语中指把情形单独拎出规则之外。经古法语 excepter 进入中古英语。

sensesIntro.en: From the hand that grabs everything, one item is released: exclusion first, then the leftover that remains.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「抓住一切」的手出发，松开一件即排除，反向看则只剩留下的那一项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one item released from a closed hand
core.cn: 核心意象：合拢的手里松开一件东西

branches.en: the item is formally left out
branches.cn: 该项被正式排除在外

branches.en: a whole clause is the released piece
branches.cn: 被松开的是一整句话

branches.en: what stays inside the hand is named
branches.cn: 点出手上仅剩的那一项

branches.en: exclusion and residue are two views of one cut
branches.cn: 排除与剩余是同一切口的两面

branches.en: the cut can limit or carve out a rule
branches.cn: 这个切口可以限定或豁免规则

intro.en: The family gathers around the Latin root cap- (take, seize) with direction prefixes.
intro.cn: 词族围绕拉丁词根 cap-（拿、抓住）加上方向前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin cousins that keep the cap- root.
latinIntro.cn: 保留 cap- 词根的拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 交换；兑换；（证券交易所等）交易场所；短暂交谈；交换所
definition_en: the act of giving one thing and receiving another in its place
core_image: 两手同时伸出，各自把东西递到对方掌心，收回时已换了一样
scene: 车站门口，两个旅客把各自的车票递过去，看对方的座位是否更靠窗。They agreed to an exchange of seats so the child could sit by the window.
sceneCN: 这里 exchange 指「两方互给互取的交换」（第 1 个义项：作为一次对等交换）；句意为他们同意换座位，好让孩子靠窗坐。

pos.zh: 交换；兑换；交易场所；短暂交谈

derivatives.zh: exchange + -able（可…的）→ 可交换的；可兑换的
inter-（相互）+ change → 互换；换乘站
interchange + -able → 可互换的
拉丁 cambiare（交换）经古法语 → 改变；零钱（同根，语义分叉为「变」）
bureau + de + change → 外币兑换处（法语借入）
exchange + -er → 交换器（如热交换器）

senses.title: Giving one thing for another
senses.definition: the act of giving something and receiving something else in return
senses.definitionCN: 给出某物并换回另一物的行为
senses.example: They agreed to an exchange of seats so the child could sit by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他们同意换座位，好让孩子靠窗坐。
senses.why: Latin ex- 'out' plus cambiare 'to barter' gives a giving out that is answered by a taking in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 ex-「出」加 cambiare「以物易物」，给出一个「给出」并由「取回」回应的动作。

senses.title: A venue for trading securities or currencies
senses.titleCN: 证券或货币的交易场所
senses.definition: an organized market where financial instruments or currencies are bought and sold
senses.definitionCN: 买卖金融工具或货币的有组织市场
senses.example: The exchange closed early when the storm cut the power.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨切断电力，交易所提前收盘。
senses.why: A place where values are exchanged takes the name of the act, and the act becomes a building.
senses.whyCN: 交换价值的地方取了动作之名，动作也就成了一座建筑。

senses.title: An exchange of letters or remarks
senses.definition: a series of communications between two parties, as an exchange of letters or views
senses.definitionCN: 两方之间一系列的书信或意见往来
senses.example: The exchange of letters lasted three years and settled nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 书信往来进行三年，什么也没解决。
senses.why: Words are given and words are returned, so correspondence is the same shape as trade.
senses.whyCN: 话被给出，话又被送回，因此通信与交易是同一个形状。

senses.title: A short argument or conversation
senses.definition: a brief, often heated, passage of talk between two people
senses.definitionCN: 两人之间一段简短、常带火气的对话
senses.example: A sharp exchange at the door ended the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 门口一场尖锐的交锋结束了这次会面。
senses.why: The countable sense shrinks a whole correspondence into one round of give and take.
senses.whyCN: 可数义把整段往来缩小为一个给出与回敬的回合。

senses.title: A telephone switchboard
senses.definition: dated technical: a building or apparatus where lines are connected by an operator
senses.definitionCN: 旧技术用语：由话务员接通线路的机房或设备
senses.example: The old exchange on the corner still has a manual board.
senses.exampleCN: 街角那间旧交换机房仍有一台人工交换台。
senses.why: Lines are exchanged between callers, and the machinery that performs the exchange takes the name.
senses.whyCN: 线路在通话者之间被交换，执行交换的机器便取了这个名字。

senses.title: A swap of captives or personnel
senses.definition: an agreed handing over of prisoners, spies or personnel by two sides
senses.definitionCN: 两方商定的战俘、间谍或人员交还
senses.example: The prisoner exchange took place at a border bridge at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 战俘交换在黎明时分的一座边境桥上进行。
senses.why: People are treated as the things given and received, which is why the plain word is used without euphemism.
senses.whyCN: 人被当作被给出与接收的对象，因此这里直用这个普通的词，不加委婉语。

senses.title: To swap (verb)
senses.definition: to give something and receive something else in return, or to give each other
senses.definitionCN: 给出某物并换回另一物，或互相给予
senses.example: The two schools exchange students every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这两所学校每年春天交换学生。
senses.why: The verb makes the noun into a repeated or mutual act.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个名词变成反复或相互的动作。

senses.title: Conversion of one currency for another
senses.definition: the changing of money of one country into that of another at a stated rate
senses.definitionCN: 按既定比价把一国货币换为另一国货币
senses.example: The exchange cost him nine percent before he left the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 他还没出机场，兑换就花掉了他百分之九。
senses.why: A money counter is the same gesture with one currency on each side, so no separate word is needed.
senses.whyCN: 换钱的柜台是同一个动作，只是两侧各放一种货币，因此无需另造新词。

senses.title: An organized programme of visits
senses.definition: a scheme in which people from two places visit each other, as a student or cultural exchange
senses.definitionCN: 两地人员互访的安排，如学生交流或文化交流
senses.example: The cultural exchange brought twelve potters to the city for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这项文化交流把十二位陶工请到城里住了一个月。
senses.why: An institution borrows the word for reciprocal visits, since each side hosts and is hosted.
senses.whyCN: 一种制度借用了这个词来指互访，因为每一方既接待也被接待。

intro.en: Exchange is a French-shaped verb from spoken Latin, and its key root is one of the least certain in this batch.
intro.cn: exchange 是一个由口语拉丁而来、带法语形态的动词，其核心词根是本批中最不确定的几个之一。

items.en: Cambiare meant 'to exchange, to barter'. Its own origin is uncertain: a link to a Celtic verb for 'change' is often suggested, but no derivation has been demonstrated.
items.cn: cambiare 意为「交换、以物易物」。它自身的来源不确定：常有人提出它与某个凯尔特语表「改变」的动词有关，但没有任何派生得到证实。

items.en: Spoken Latin added ex- 'out' to cambiare, producing *excambiare 'to exchange out, to swap'.
items.cn: 口语拉丁给 cambiare 加上 ex-「出」，构成 *excambiare「换出、交换」。

items.en: Old French eschangier continues the spoken form and supplies the -ch- that English preserves in the noun.
items.cn: 古法语 eschangier 承接口语形式，并提供英语名词中保留的那个 -ch-。

items.en: English borrows the word in the fourteenth century as both noun and verb, first for swapping goods and then for money changing.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪把这个词作为名词与动词一并借入，先指换货，后指换钱。

items.en: The financial sense develops with the rise of the bourse: a place where bills and currencies are exchanged becomes simply the exchange.
items.cn: 金融义随交易所的兴起而发展：买卖票据与货币的场所干脆就被称作 the exchange。

items.en: The telephone exchange extends the word to a room where lines are connected, a sense now largely historical.
items.cn: 电话交换机把这个词扩展到接通线路的机房，这一义项如今大体已成历史。

note.en: The first group shares the root or the shape and is easily confused; the second holds words for swaps and for trading venues.
note.cn: 第一组共享词根或外形，容易混淆；第二组是交换行为与交易场所的其他说法。

entries.definition: The short form of the same Latin root, but it means to become different as well as to swap; exchange keeps only the two-way giving.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁词根的短形式，但除交换外还指「变得不同」；exchange 只保留双向给予之义。

entries.definition: Inter- 'between' plus change marks a two-way swap, and in transport it names a junction where routes swap passengers.
entries.definitionCN: inter-「之间」加 change 标出双向互换，在交通中指路线互换乘客的枢纽。

entries.definition: The adjective means able to be swapped or converted, often in economics or law rather than in daily speech.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词指可交换或可兑换，多见于经济或法律语境而非日常口语。

entries.definition: A tax on goods, from a different Latin source (ex- plus caedere 'to cut'); it has nothing to do with swapping.
entries.definitionCN: 指货物税，来自另一个拉丁来源（ex- 加 caedere「切」），与交换无关。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a mutual exchange, usually of similar things and often without paperwork.
entries.definitionCN: 互相交换的日常用词，通常换同类之物，且常无手续。

entries.definition: An exchange carried on as business, especially of goods; exchange is neutral about whether money is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 作为生意的交换，尤指货物；exchange 不限定是否涉及钱。

entries.definition: Exchange with no money at all; it is one strict kind of exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 完全不用钱的交换，是 exchange 的一个严格子类。

entries.definition: Changing one thing into another form, often without a second party; exchange requires someone on the other side.
entries.definitionCN: 把一物变为另一形式，常无第二方；exchange 则要求对面有人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + cambiare 'barter': hand something out and take something in.
normal.cn: ex-「出」+ cambiare「以物易物」：把东西递出去，再收一件回来。

normal.en: The family runs exchange, exchangeable, interchange, interchangeable, changer, change.
normal.cn: 同族词有 exchange、exchangeable、interchange、interchangeable、changer、change。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the venues: stock exchange, exchange rate, labour exchange, telephone exchange.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出场所：证券交易所、汇率、职业介绍所、电话交换机。

normal.en: The verb is mutual: two schools exchange students, and each is host and guest.
normal.cn: 动词是相互的：两校交换学生，各自既是主人也是客人。

normal.en: Words exchange too: an exchange of views is correspondence with the same shape.
normal.cn: 话也能交换：交换意见就是同形状的往来。

abstract.en: Picture two palms opening at the same moment, each now holding what the other had.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手掌同时张开，各自握着对方原来拿的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a building with no goods in it, only numbers being swapped all day.
abstract.cn: 想象一座里面没有货物、整天只在交换数字的建筑。

abstract.en: Picture an operator plugging a line into a socket so two strangers can talk.
abstract.cn: 想象话务员把一根线插进插孔，好让两个陌生人通话。

examples.en: The two museums arranged an exchange of paintings for a season.
examples.cn: 两家博物馆安排了一季的绘画互换。

examples.en: He exchanged his seat for a place by the aisle and slept the whole way.
examples.cn: 他换到靠过道的座位，一路睡了过去。

examples.en: The exchange rate moved two percent before the markets opened.
examples.cn: 开市之前，汇率已经动了两成中的两个百分点。

dict_mnemonic.text: ex（出）+ change（换）＝ 把东西换出去，换回一样；先记「两只手同时递」，再记「一所房子专门换数字」。

root: 拉丁 cambiare「交换、以物易物」+ ex-「出」→ 口语拉丁 *excambiare → 古法语 eschangier → 英语 exchange；cambiare 来源不确定，与凯尔特语的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one gesture of give and take: a swap, a hall of swaps, words swapped, one sharp round of words, a switchboard, captives handed over, the verb, currency conversion, and a programme of mutual visits.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一个「递出与接回」的动作展开：一次交换、专门交换的场所、交换话语、一个尖锐的话语回合、交换机、交出俘虏、动词、货币兑换，以及互访项目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands opening at once, each receiving exactly what the other releases.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手同时张开，各自接到的正是对方松开的。

branches.en: THE GESTURE AND THE VERB: one completed swap, then the same act performed habitually or mutually.
branches.cn: 动作与动词：一次完成的交换，再是同一动作被反复或相互地做。

branches.en: PLACES AND MACHINES OF SWAPPING: a hall for securities, a room for telephone lines, a counter for currencies.
branches.cn: 交换的场所与机器：换证券的大厅、接线路的机房、换货币的柜台。

branches.en: WORDS IN PLACE OF GOODS: correspondence over years, or one sharp round at a door.
branches.cn: 以话代货：经年的通信，或门口一个尖锐的回合。

branches.en: PEOPLE HANDED OVER: the plain word is used without euphemism for prisoners.
branches.cn: 被交出的人：对俘虏直接用这个普通的词，不加委婉。

branches.en: AN INSTITUTION OF HOSTING: each side gives a visit and receives one, so a programme becomes an exchange.
branches.cn: 接待的制度：每一方给出一次访问也收到一次，于是项目本身成了 exchange。

intro.en: Exchange is one Latin prefix plus one uncertain Latin verb, and both parts recur in English words about movement and substitution.
intro.cn: exchange 是一个拉丁前缀加一个来源不确定的拉丁动词，两部分在英语中反复出现于表移动与替代的词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin cambiare 'to barter' gives change, exchange, interchange and the money-changing phrases; ex- 'out' recurs in exit, export and extract. The root behind cambiare is not established.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cambiare「以物易物」给出 change、exchange、interchange 与换钱的短语；ex-「出」在 exit、export、extract 中重现。cambiare 之后的词根未得到证实。

definition_zh: 使激动；激起；刺激；引发
definition_en: to make someone feel strong emotion, or to cause a feeling or reaction to arise
core_image: 往平静的水面丢一块石头：涟漪一圈圈荡出去，水面再也静不下来
scene: 开学第一天老师宣布全班要去参观科技馆，教室里立刻响起一片欢呼，老师笑着说：The news excited every student in the class.
sceneCN: 这里 excite 指「使人产生强烈情绪」（第 1 个义项：让内心激动起来）；句意为这个消息让全班学生都很兴奋。

derivatives.zh: 令人兴奋的（excite 的现在分词作形容词，指「让人激动起来的」）
感到兴奋的（过去分词作形容词，指「被激起情绪的」）
兴奋；激动（excite 加名词后缀 -ment，义为「被激起的情绪状态」）
易激动的（excite 加形容词后缀 -able，义为「容易被点着的」）

senses.title: To stir up strong feeling
senses.definition: to cause someone to feel excitement, joy, fear, or another strong emotion
senses.definitionCN: 让人心里生出兴奋、喜悦、害怕等强烈的情绪
senses.example: The news excited every student in the class.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息让全班学生都很兴奋。
senses.why: A stone in still water: the outer event touches the calm surface, and feeling ripples out from the centre.
senses.whyCN: 一块石头落进静水：外来的事件碰到平静的表面，情绪便从中心荡开。

senses.title: To arouse interest or curiosity
senses.definition: to make people interested, curious, or eager to know more
senses.definitionCN: 让人产生兴趣、好奇或想一探究竟
senses.example: The mystery excited the reader's curiosity.
senses.exampleCN: 这个谜团激起了读者的好奇心。
senses.why: The same ripple reaches the mind: the event stirs questions instead of emotions.
senses.whyCN: 同样的涟漪也能荡到头脑里：事件这次激起的是问题而非情绪。

senses.title: To trigger a physical or chemical response
senses.titleCN: 触发身体的或化学的反应
senses.definition: to cause a nerve, organ, or substance to become active
senses.definitionCN: 让神经、器官或物质进入活动状态
senses.example: The electric current excited the nerve cells.
senses.exampleCN: 电流激活了这些神经细胞。
senses.why: The image becomes technical: instead of people, cells and currents are the water that gets stirred.
senses.whyCN: 画面变得专业：被搅动的不再是人，而是细胞与电流这片「水」。

senses.title: To cause unrest or public controversy
senses.definition: to stir up public feeling, protest, or unrest
senses.definitionCN: 激起公众的情绪、抗议或骚乱
senses.example: The unfair rule excited anger across the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这条不公的规定激起了全城的愤怒。
senses.why: When the ripples spread through a whole crowd, the stirred water is society itself.
senses.whyCN: 当涟漪扩散到整个人群，被搅动的那片水就是社会本身。

intro.en: Excite comes from a Latin verb about calling something out, and French carried it into English.
intro.cn: excite 源自拉丁语「把某物唤出来」的动词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Latin excitare meant "to call out, to rouse, to stir up", an intensive form of ciere "to move, to summon".
items.cn: 拉丁语 excitare 意为「唤出、唤起、搅动」，是 ciere「使动、召唤」的加强形式。

items.en: The image is calling a sleeping thing awake: a bell rung to make the water move.
items.cn: 画面是把沉睡的东西叫醒：像敲钟让水面动起来。

items.en: Old French had exciter with the same senses of rousing feeling and provoking action.
items.cn: 古法语作 exciter，保留「唤起情绪」「引发行动」两义。

items.en: Middle English borrowed exciten in the fourteenth century, first for rousing people to action.
items.cn: 十四世纪中古英语借入 exciten，最初用于唤起人去行动。

items.en: Modern English widened it from stirring people to stirring interest, nerves, and crowds.
items.cn: 现代英语把适用面从「唤起人」扩大到兴趣、神经与人群。

note.en: These neighbours share spelling or the idea of stirring something up.
note.cn: 下列词与 excite 拼写相近，或同样有「把东西搅起来」的意思。

normalIntro.en: Five associations from the real root and common usage.
normalIntro.cn: 五条来自真实词根与常用法的联想。

normal.en: ex- (out) + cite (call): you call a feeling out of its quiet hiding place.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex-（向外）+ 词根 cite（唤）：把情绪从安静处「叫出来」。

normal.en: Excited vs exciting: you are excited, the film is exciting.
normal.cn: excited 说人被点燃，exciting 说东西会点燃人。

normal.en: Excitement is the mood itself: the crowd buzzed with excitement.
normal.cn: excitement 是情绪本身：人群兴奋地嗡嗡作响。

normal.en: Cite and recite are cousins: both call words out.
normal.cn: cite 与 recite 是近亲：都把词「唤出」。

normal.en: Excitable people are easy stones to drop in water.
normal.cn: excitable 的人是容易被丢石子起涟漪的那种水面。

abstract.en: Picture a flat pond: one stone lands and rings of feeling spread outward.
abstract.cn: 想象一片平湖：石子落下，情绪的圆环向外扩散。

abstract.en: A sleeping crowd is still water; a speech can wake it into waves.
abstract.cn: 沉睡的人群是静水，一场演讲能让它掀起波浪。

abstract.en: Emotion in this word is motion: to excite is literally to set feeling in motion.
abstract.cn: 这个词里情绪即运动：excite 的本义就是让情绪动起来。

examples.cn: 这个消息让全班学生都很兴奋。

examples.en: The electric current excited the nerve cells.
examples.cn: 电流激活了这些神经细胞。

sensesIntro.cn: 从「把情绪从平静中唤出」出发，覆盖到头脑、神经与人群。

branches.cn: 个人或人群中被激起的强烈情绪

definition_zh: 兴奋；激动；刺激；令人兴奋的事
definition_en: a feeling of great eagerness or strong emotion, or something that produces this feeling
core_image: 开场铃响前挤满人的游乐场：心跳加速，谁也站不住
scene: 游乐园的过山车缓缓爬到最高点，车厢里所有人屏住呼吸，随后尖叫声混着笑声炸开，谁也安静不下来。The excitement of the ride kept him buzzing all afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 excitement 指「强烈的兴奋情绪」（第 1 个义项：又期待又紧张的心理状态）；句意为过山车的刺激让他整个下午都兴奋难平。

derivatives.zh: 使激动；激起（excitement 的动词根，义为「把情绪唤出来」）

senses.title: The state of strong eagerness
senses.definition: a state of feeling excited, eager, and often unable to stay calm
senses.definitionCN: 既期待又紧张、难以保持平静的心理状态
senses.example: The excitement of the ride kept him buzzing all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 游乐设施的刺激让他整个下午都兴奋难平。
senses.why: The suffix -ment turns the verb into a thing: the stirred water becomes the swirling you can feel inside.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 把动词变成名词：被搅动的水面变成体内能感觉到的翻腾。

senses.title: Something that causes strong feeling
senses.definition: an event or thing that produces excitement
senses.definitionCN: 会让人兴奋起来的事件或事物
senses.example: The trip added a new excitement to the quiet summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这次旅行给安静的夏天添了一份新刺激。
senses.why: Once the feeling is a noun, it can also mean its own source: the stir names both the wave and the stone.
senses.whyCN: 情绪成为名词后也可指其来源：这个词既指波浪，也指石头。

senses.title: Public unrest or turmoil
senses.definition: a situation of public agitation or nervous activity
senses.definitionCN: 公众情绪被搅起、人心不稳的局面
senses.example: The rumour caused great excitement in the town.
senses.exampleCN: 谣言在镇上引起了极大的骚动。
senses.why: When many waters ripple at once, the name covers the social storm too.
senses.whyCN: 当许多水面同时起波澜，这个词也覆盖了社会层面的风暴。

intro.en: Excitement is the verb excite plus the noun suffix -ment, formed in English from Latin stock.
intro.cn: excitement 即动词 excite 加名词后缀 -ment，在英语中由拉丁词干构成。

items.en: The root is excitare "to rouse", from ciere "to move, to summon".
items.cn: 词根是 excitare「唤起」，来自 ciere「使动、召唤」。

items.en: French had exciter and excitements, carrying both feeling and agitation.
items.cn: 法语有 exciter 与 excitements，兼指情绪与骚动。

items.en: The noun excitements appears in English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 excitements 于十五世纪见于英语。

items.en: Modern English uses it mainly for the feeling, with the older unrest sense kept in formal prose.
items.cn: 现代英语主要用于情绪义，骚动义保留在正式文体中。

items.en: The -ment suffix marks the result state: after the stone falls, this is what the water does.
items.cn: 后缀 -ment 标记结果状态：石落之后，水面由此翻腾。

note.en: Nearby nouns name similar stirred-up states of mind.
note.cn: 相邻名词同样指被搅起的心理状态。

scene: 迟到的学生站在教室门口，书包还没放下就急着开口，老师摆摆手说：A heavy rain on the road is a reasonable excuse for being late.
sceneCN: 这里 excuse 指「用来脱责的理由」（第 1 个义项：为过错开脱的说法）；句意为路上大雨是迟到的合理解释。

derivatives.zh: 可原谅的（excuse 加 -able，义为「可以被搬开责任的」）
不可原谅的（in- 加 excusable，义为「责任搬不开的」）
表示原谅的；开脱的（现在分词作形容词）

senses.title: A reason offered to explain a fault
senses.definition: a reason given to explain or justify a mistake or failure
senses.definitionCN: 为错误或失败给出的解释或辩护理由
senses.example: A heavy rain on the road is a reasonable excuse for being late.
senses.exampleCN: 路上下大雨是迟到的合理解释。
senses.why: The Latin root is to hold blame away from someone: the story told does exactly this work for the person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根是「把罪责从某人身上拿开」：说出的说法正是在替人做这件事。

senses.title: A false or weak justification
senses.definition: a weak or untrue reason used to hide the real cause
senses.definitionCN: 用来掩盖真实原因的勉强或不实的理由
senses.example: Stop making excuses and start practising.
senses.exampleCN: 别再找借口了，开始练习吧。
senses.why: When the story only pretends to carry the blame away, the same word marks it as a shelter, not a reason.
senses.whyCN: 当说法只是假装搬开责任，同一个词就把它标记为遮掩而非理由。

senses.title: To forgive a fault or offence
senses.definition: to overlook or forgive someone's mistake or bad behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 不计较、原谅某人的错误或失礼
senses.example: Please excuse my late reply.
senses.exampleCN: 请原谅我回复晚了。
senses.why: As a verb, the hand actively lifts the blame off the other person's shoulder.
senses.whyCN: 作为动词，那只手主动把责任从对方肩上拿开。

senses.title: To free someone from a duty or presence
senses.definition: to release someone from a duty, or politely allow them to leave
senses.definitionCN: 把某人从职责中放出，或礼貌地允许其离开
senses.example: The teacher excused the sick student from PE class.
senses.exampleCN: 老师准许生病的学生不上体育课。
senses.why: The same lifting hand can remove a burden that is not guilt at all, only a requirement.
senses.whyCN: 同一只抬手也能搬走根本不是罪责的东西——只是一项要求。

intro.en: Excuse goes back to Latin ex- (out) + causa (charge, accusation): literally to set the charge aside.
intro.cn: excuse 可追溯至拉丁语 ex-（向外）+ causa（指控）：字面义是「把指控挪开」。

items.en: Late Latin excusare meant "to free from blame", built on causa "a charge, a court case".
items.cn: 后期拉丁语 excusare 意为「使人免于罪责」，建立在 causa「指控、讼案」之上。

items.en: Causa also gave English cause; excuse is literally the act of removing a legal cause of complaint.
items.cn: causa 也衍生出英语 cause；excuse 字面上就是移除一桩法律上的控诉事由。

items.en: Old French excuser carried the verb into Romance speech with the same legal flavour.
items.cn: 古法语 excuser 以同样的法律色彩把动词带入罗曼语。

items.en: Middle English borrowed it in the thirteenth century, noun and verb arriving together.
items.cn: 十三世纪中古英语借入该词，名词与动词同时进入。

items.en: Modern English split the stress: EXcuse is the reason, exCUSE the forgiving act.
items.cn: 现代英语分化重音：EXcuse 是理由，exCUSE 是原谅的动作。

note.en: These neighbours share the spelling frame or the act of setting blame aside.
note.cn: 下列词与 excuse 拼写框架相同，或同样有「把责任放一边」的动作。

definition_en: activity done to practise, to train the body, or to make use of a power, right, or quality
core_image: 反复推动磨刀石：身体与技能都在一次次重复中被磨亮
scene: 清晨的公园里，老人在树下慢慢打拳，年轻人在跑道上一圈圈跑着，教练喊道：Daily exercise keeps both your body and your mind sharp.
sceneCN: 这里 exercise 指「为强身而做的运动」（第 2 个义项：锻炼身体的身体活动）；句意为每天锻炼能让身体和头脑都保持敏锐。

derivatives.zh: 锻炼者；健身器（exercise 加表示施动者的 -er）
发挥；施加（同源词，义为「把力量推出去」）

senses.title: A task for practising a skill
senses.definition: a set task done repeatedly to learn or improve a skill
senses.definitionCN: 为学会或提高某项技能而反复做的指定任务
senses.example: Finish exercise five on page twelve before Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 周五前完成第十二页的第五题。
senses.why: The root image is driving a skill forward by repetition: each task is one push of the wheel.
senses.whyCN: 词根画面是通过重复推动技能：每道题都是推一次磨盘。

senses.title: Bodily activity for health
senses.definition: physical movement done to keep the body strong and healthy
senses.definitionCN: 为保持身体强健而做的身体活动
senses.example: Daily exercise keeps both your body and your mind sharp.
senses.exampleCN: 每天锻炼能让身体和头脑都保持敏锐。
senses.why: The body is the skill being trained: the same repetition now polishes muscles and breath.
senses.whyCN: 此时被训练的「技能」是身体：同样的重复磨亮的是肌肉与呼吸。

senses.title: To use a power, right, or quality
senses.definition: to make active use of a power, right, ability, or quality
senses.definitionCN: 实际动用某项权力、权利、能力或品质
senses.example: Citizens exercise the right to vote in elections.
senses.exampleCN: 公民在选举中行使投票权。
senses.why: The driving force turns inward-to-outward: the power is pushed out through action, like strength pushed through a lever.
senses.whyCN: 驱动力由内向外：力量通过行动被推出，如同力气压过杠杆。

senses.title: To worry or occupy the mind
senses.definition: to make someone anxious or thoughtful about something
senses.definitionCN: 让某人对某事放心不下或反复思量
senses.example: The delay began to exercise the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 延误开始让全队焦虑起来。
senses.why: The pushing image applies to the mind: worry pushes thoughts round and round like the wheel.
senses.whyCN: 推磨的画面用到头脑上：忧虑让念头像磨盘一样转个不停。

senses.title: A formal military or training activity
senses.definition: a planned activity, often military, for practising procedures
senses.definitionCN: 为演练流程而安排的活动，常见于军事
senses.example: Thousands of soldiers joined the exercise near the border.
senses.exampleCN: 数千名士兵参加了边境附近的演习。
senses.why: When whole teams repeat together, the single practice becomes a large staged rehearsal.
senses.whyCN: 当整支队伍共同重复，单项练习就成了大规模的排演。

intro.en: Exercise comes from Latin ex- (out) + arcere (to keep off, to enclose), originally "to drive out of an enclosure".
intro.cn: exercise 源自拉丁语 ex-（向外）+ arcere（拦住、圈住），本义为「把牲口赶出圈外」。

items.en: Latin exercere meant "to drive out of the enclosure, to train", used of driving draft animals and drilling troops.
items.cn: 拉丁语 exercere 意为「赶出圈外、训练」，既用于驱赶役畜，也用于操练军队。

items.en: The training image grew from this: work repeated until the animal or soldier is fit.
items.cn: 训练义由此生长：重复劳作，直到牲口或士兵胜任。

items.en: Old French exercice carried the noun into Romance, meaning practice and training.
items.cn: 古法语 exercice 以名词形式传入罗曼语，意为练习与训练。

items.en: Middle English took exercice in the fourteenth century for both drill and physical activity.
items.cn: 十四世纪中古英语借入 exercice，兼指操练与身体活动。

items.en: Modern English added the legal use of exercising rights and the old sense of troubling the mind.
items.cn: 现代英语添入了行使权利的法律用法，并保留「使心神不安」的古义。

definition_en: a public show of objects, artworks, or skills, or the act of showing something

senses.title: A public display of objects or artworks
senses.definition: an organized public showing of paintings, objects, or collections
senses.definitionCN: 把画作、物品或收藏有组织地向公众展示
senses.example: The new exhibition opens to the public this Saturday.
senses.exampleCN: 新展览本周六对公众开放。
senses.why: The root is to hold something out for seeing: here a whole room is arranged so everything can be held out at once.
senses.whyCN: 词根是「把东西递出来给人看」：这里整间屋子被布置成能同时展出一切的场地。

senses.title: The act of showing a quality
senses.definition: the act of showing a feeling, skill, or quality openly
senses.definitionCN: 公开显露某种情感、技艺或品质
senses.example: The match was an exhibition of pure skill.
senses.exampleCN: 这场比赛是一场纯技艺的展示。
senses.why: When the displayed thing is not an object but an ability, the showing itself is the event.
senses.whyCN: 当被展出的是能力而非实物，展示行为本身就成了「展览」。

senses.title: An exhibition match or performance
senses.definition: a match or performance played to demonstrate skill rather than to decide a winner
senses.definitionCN: 为展示技艺而非决出胜负而进行的比赛或演出
senses.example: The champions played an exhibition game for the fans.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军队为球迷打了一场表演赛。
senses.why: A display needs no stakes: the game is staged only to be looked at, like any exhibit.
senses.whyCN: 展示不需要赌注：这场比赛只为了被看，就像任何展品一样。

senses.title: A grant or exhibition of money
senses.titleCN: 奖学金；津贴（英式旧用法）
senses.definition: in British use, a sum of money awarded to a student
senses.definitionCN: 英式用法中指发给学生的奖助学金
senses.example: She won an exhibition to study at Oxford.
senses.exampleCN: 她获得了一项资助赴牛津学习的奖学金。
senses.why: An old formal sense: the award is laid out for the student's benefit, like items laid out for viewing.
senses.whyCN: 一个古老的正式义：这笔资助被「摆出」供学生受用，如同展品被摆出供人看。

intro.en: Exhibition is the noun of exhibit, from Latin ex- (out) + habere (to hold): to hold out for viewing.
intro.cn: exhibition 是 exhibit 的名词，源自拉丁语 ex-（向外）+ habere（持有）：把东西「拿出来给人看」。

items.en: Latin exhibere meant "to hold out, to present", from ex- (out) + habere (to hold, to have).
items.cn: 拉丁语 exhibere 意为「递出、呈示」，由 ex-（向外）+ habere（持、有）构成。

items.en: The picture is a hand extending an object toward the viewer's eyes.
items.cn: 画面是一只手把物件递到观看者眼前。

items.en: Medieval legal use made exhibere mean to submit a document for inspection.
items.cn: 中世纪法律用法让 exhibere 指「提交文件供查验」。

items.en: Middle English took exhibition in the fourteenth century, first as the act of presenting.
items.cn: 十四世纪中古英语借入 exhibition，最初指「呈递」这一行为。

items.en: The public-show sense grew in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries with museums and art salons.
items.cn: 「公开展览」义随十七、十八世纪博物馆与艺术沙龙兴起而成熟。
