normal.en: ex- (out) + hibit (hold): hold the painting out where all can see.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex-（向外）+ 词根 hibit（持）：把画递到人人可见之处。

normal.en: Exhibit is the verb and the item; exhibition is the whole event.
normal.cn: exhibit 是动词也是展品，exhibition 是整场活动。

normal.en: Inhibit and prohibit hold things back; exhibition holds them out.
normal.cn: inhibit 与 prohibit 把东西按住，exhibition 把东西递出。

normal.en: An exhibition match exists only to be watched.
normal.cn: 表演赛只为被观看而存在。

normal.en: Exhibition hall is where the holding-out happens in bulk.
normal.cn: exhibition hall 就是大批「递出」发生的场地。

abstract.en: Picture a gallery wall: each frame is a hand offering one image.
abstract.cn: 想象画廊的墙：每只画框都是一只递出图像的手。

abstract.en: Showing a skill is hanging an invisible painting where judges can see.
abstract.cn: 展示技艺就是挂一幅看不见的画给评委看。

abstract.en: The word family splits by direction: out (exhibit) versus back (inhibit).
abstract.cn: 词族按方向分工：向外是 exhibit，按住是 inhibit。

examples.en: The new exhibition opens to the public this Saturday.
examples.cn: 新展览本周六对公众开放。

examples.en: The match was an exhibition of pure skill.
examples.cn: 这场比赛是一场纯技艺的展示。

examples.en: She won an exhibition to study at Oxford.
examples.cn: 她获得了一项资助赴牛津学习的奖学金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱克瑟比身」——把自己最好的作品摆出来给众人「比一比、看一看」。

root: 源自拉丁语 exhibere「递出、呈示」，由 ex-（向外）+ habere（持、有）构成；经法语与中古英语，公开展示义在近代成熟。与 inhibit、prohibit 同享 habere 词根。

sensesIntro.en: From holding an object out to view, the word grows into displays of skill and even student grants.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「把物件递出供看」出发，扩展到技艺展示乃至学生奖助金。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holding an object out for eyes to see
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把物件递到众人眼前

branches.en: rooms arranged so objects are held out at scale
branches.cn: 整间屋子按「递出」逻辑布置

branches.en: skills displayed like objects on a wall
branches.cn: 技艺如展品般被挂出

branches.en: a game staged purely for viewing
branches.cn: 只为观看而 staged 的比赛

branches.en: money laid out for a student's benefit
branches.cn: 资助被「摆出」供学生受用

branches.en: public showing is the shared core
branches.cn: 公开展示是共同的核

intro.en: The family sits on Latin habere (hold) with direction prefixes that flip the meaning.
intro.cn: 词族建立在拉丁 habere（持）上，方向前缀反转词义。

latinIntro.en: Latin cousins from the habere root.
latinIntro.cn: habere 词根的拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 期待；预计；要求；料想；怀有身孕
definition_en: to believe that something will happen, to await it, or to require it as a duty
core_image: 一个人站在门口向外望，手里已经握住门把
scene: 站台上，家长不断看表，孩子乘坐的列车还有十分钟到站。She did not expect the train to be so crowded.
sceneCN: 这里 expect 指「料想某事会发生」（第 1 个义项：认为某事将会发生）；句意为他没想到列车会这么拥挤。场景要素：站台、看表的手、到站显示屏。

derivatives.zh: 由 expect 加名词后缀构成，指预期或期望的事物
由 expect 加过去分词词尾构成，指按计划应当发生的
由否定前缀加 expected 构成，指出乎意料的
由 expect 加形容词后缀构成，指期待着的或即将为人父母的
由 expectant 加副词后缀构成，指以期待的神情

senses.title: Believe something will happen
senses.definition: to think that an event is likely to happen, on the basis of evidence or habit
senses.definitionCN: 基于证据或习惯，认为某事件很可能会发生
senses.example: Economists expect a slight fall in exports this quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家预计本季度出口会小幅下降。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to look out for, so the modern verb is that watch turned into a claim about the future.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「向外张望」，因此现代动词就是那种张望变成了对未来的断言。

senses.title: Await an arrival
senses.definition: to be waiting for a person or thing that is due to come
senses.definitionCN: 正在等候按计划要来的人或物
senses.example: We expect the auditors at nine and the courier before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 我们等审计人员九点到，快递中午前到。
senses.why: Waiting is the original physical sense, and it survives whenever the object is a person or a delivery rather than a fact.
senses.whyCN: 等待是最初的具体义，只要对象是人或送来的东西而非事实，它就仍然成立。

senses.title: Require as a duty
senses.definition: to require something of someone because a rule, role or standard demands it
senses.definitionCN: 因规则、身份或标准而要求某人做到某事
senses.example: The school expects students to cite every source.
senses.exampleCN: 学校要求学生为每一处来源标注出处。
senses.why: A prediction about a person's behaviour easily becomes an obligation, which is how the demanding sense grew out of the forecasting one.
senses.whyCN: 对人的行为所作预判很容易变成义务，要求的义项就是这样从预判义长出来的。

senses.title: Suppose without certainty
senses.definition: to suppose or guess, often marked as uncertain in speech
senses.definitionCN: 推测或猜想，口语中常带不确定的标记
senses.example: I expect you have already heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 我猜你已经听说这个消息了。
senses.why: When the evidence is thin, the same verb softens into mere supposition, and English marks this with a plain declarative tone.
senses.whyCN: 证据不足时，同一个动词软化为单纯的推测，英语靠平直的陈述语气来标出这一点。

senses.title: Be expecting a baby
senses.definition: in the progressive, to be pregnant
senses.definitionCN: 用于进行时，指正在怀孕
senses.example: She is expecting in early spring and has already told her team.
senses.exampleCN: 她初春就要生产，已经告诉了团队。
senses.why: The waiting sense is applied to a birth, and English uses the progressive as a polite stand-in for the word pregnant.
senses.whyCN: 等待义被用到生产上，英语用进行时作为「怀孕」的委婉说法。

senses.title: Forecast in figures
senses.definition: to forecast a quantity, as analysts do with prices, demand or earnings
senses.definitionCN: 像分析师对价格、需求或收益那样预测一个数量
senses.example: Analysts expect inflation to stay above target until winter.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师预计通胀会一直高于目标直到冬季。
senses.why: Once the object is a number, the verb belongs to forecasting, and the sentence reads as a projection rather than a hope.
senses.whyCN: 一旦对象是数字，这个动词就属于预测语境，句子读起来是投影而非愿望。

senses.title: Require much of someone
senses.definition: to demand a high level of effort or behaviour from someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的努力或表现提出很高要求
senses.example: The coach expects a great deal from the senior rowers.
senses.exampleCN: 教练对资深桨手要求很高。
senses.why: The demanding sense intensifies when the standard is high, and the verb then describes pressure rather than prediction.
senses.whyCN: 标准一高，要求的义项就加重，这个动词于是描述压力而不是预判。

senses.title: Be due to arrive
senses.definition: to be scheduled or due, as a train or flight is
senses.definitionCN: 如列车或航班那样，按安排应当到达
senses.example: The flight is expected at half past six, weather permitting.
senses.exampleCN: 天气允许的话，这班飞机预计六点半到。
senses.why: Schedules turned the verb into a passive formula, which is why stations and airports use it for anything with a timetable.
senses.whyCN: 时刻表把这个动词变成了被动套语，因此车站与机场用它指任何有时间表的事物。

intro.en: Expect comes from Latin exspectare 'to look out for', a prefix meaning 'out' plus a frequentative verb for looking. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: expect 来自拉丁语 exspectare「向外张望」，由表「向外」的前缀加一个表示反复看的动词构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: The prefix meant 'out, outward', aiming the gaze beyond the present spot.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为「向外、出去」，把目光投向当下位置之外。

items.en: Spectare 'to look at' was built on the verb for seeing; the deeper origin of that verb is not established.
items.cn: spectare「看」建立在表「看见」的动词上；那个动词的更早来源未得到证明。

items.en: The compound meant 'to look out for, await', and it already carried both the watching and the believing.
items.cn: 这个复合动词意为「向外张望、等待」，已经同时带着「看」与「相信」。

items.en: The verb reached English in the fourteenth century, and the sense of requiring something of a person appears by the sixteenth.
items.cn: 这个动词在十四世纪进入英语，而「对人提出要求」的义项到十六世纪才出现。

items.en: Timetables gave the passive formula for arrivals, and the progressive became a standard way to say that someone is pregnant.
items.cn: 时刻表给出了关于到达的被动套语，进行时则成为说某人怀孕的常用方式。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the earliest English use is recorded only approximately, and the pre-Latin origin of the verb for seeing is unsettled, so any older form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：最早的英语用例只有约略记载；那个表「看见」的动词在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论，凡为其提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words and the near look-alike that share the looking verb; group two holds near neighbours for waiting and for requiring.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词以及共用「看」这一动词的近形词；第二组是表示等待与要求的近义词。

entries.definition: The noun for the belief or the standard; the verb needs a subject and a clause where the noun needs only a possessive.
entries.definitionCN: 指信念或标准的名词；动词需要主语与从句，而名词只需所有格。

entries.definition: An adjective describing someone already in a waiting state; the verb describes the act of forecasting.
entries.definitionCN: 形容已处在等待状态的人；动词描述的是预判这一行为。

entries.definition: Built with a prefix meaning 'in, into' plus the same looking root, so it means examining closely, not awaiting.
entries.definitionCN: 由表「向内」的前缀加同一个「看」词根构成，意为仔细检查而非等待。

entries.definition: Built with a prefix meaning 'back' plus the same root, so it originally meant looking back with regard; it has no forecasting sense.
entries.definitionCN: 由表「向后」的前缀加同一词根构成，原指回头看重，并无预判义。

entries.definition: To expect something and often to act in advance because of it; the English verb stresses the preparation, not the belief.
entries.definitionCN: 指预料某事，且常因此提前行动；这个英语动词强调准备而非信念。

entries.definition: A formal verb for waiting on a person or event; it carries no forecasting claim about whether the thing will come.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，指等候某人或某事；它并不断言那件事是否真会来。

entries.definition: To assume something for the sake of argument or in the absence of proof; expect is usually stronger.
entries.definitionCN: 指为讨论起见或在无证据时假定某事；expect 通常更强。

entries.definition: To demand something as necessary, often with authority; expect only implies a demand when context supplies the authority.
entries.definitionCN: 指凭借权威要求某事为必需；expect 只有在语境给出权威时才含要求。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real prefix, the real looking root, the real family and the real patterns.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的前缀、表「看」的词根、真实的词族与真实的句式。

normal.en: The Latin verb means to look out for, so expecting is keeping watch in advance.
normal.cn: 那个拉丁动词意为「向外张望」，因此期待就是提前守住目光。

normal.en: The looking root also builds spectator, inspect, respect and spectacle.
normal.cn: 表「看」的词根还构成 spectator、inspect、respect 与 spectacle。

normal.en: The family runs expect, expected, unexpected, expectant, expectation, expectancy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 expect、expected、unexpected、expectant、expectation、expectancy。

normal.en: The common patterns are expect to do and expect somebody to do.
normal.cn: 常见句式是「预计做某事」与「指望某人做某事」。

normal.en: The progressive be expecting is the polite way to say pregnant.
normal.cn: 进行时说法是「怀孕」的委婉表达。

abstract.en: Picture a hand already on the door handle before the knock comes.
abstract.cn: 想象敲门声还没响，手已经握在门把上。

abstract.en: Picture a timetable that announces a train nobody can see yet.
abstract.cn: 想象时刻表宣布一班还看不见的列车。

abstract.en: Picture a teacher who writes the standard on the board before the work starts.
abstract.cn: 想象老师在开工前先把标准写在黑板上。

examples.en: We expect the results by Friday, though the lab has not promised anything.
examples.cn: 我们预计周五前出结果，尽管实验室并未承诺。

examples.en: She expects her students to question every figure they are given.
examples.cn: 她要求学生质疑给到他们的每一个数字。

examples.en: The concert is expected to start twenty minutes late.
examples.cn: 音乐会预计晚二十分钟开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「向外看」——把目光提前投出去等结果，就是期待与预计

root: 拉丁 exspectare「向外张望」由意为「向外」的前缀加 spectare（反复看）；spectare 出自表「看见」的词根，该词根更深来源不确定。英语 expect。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one watch: looking out for what is coming. The watch becomes a forecast, then a wait, then a rule imposed on someone, then a bare guess, then a pregnancy, then a projection in figures, then a high demand, and finally a line on a timetable.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一道目光展开：向外张望将要到来之物。这道目光依次变成预判、等候、加于他人的规矩、纯然的猜测、怀孕、以数字作出的投影、很高的要求，最后是时刻表上的一行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a doorway looking outward with a hand already on the handle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在门口向外望，手已经握在门把上。

branches.en: FORECAST: a plain belief about the future and a projection in figures are the same claim at different precision.
branches.cn: 预判：对未来的朴素信念与以数字作出的投影，是同一断言的不同精度。

branches.en: WAITING: awaiting a guest and a flight due on a timetable are the watch made concrete.
branches.cn: 等待：等客人，与等时刻表上的航班，都是那道目光的具体化。

branches.en: DEMAND: a rule imposed on someone and a high standard set for them are expectation turned into pressure.
branches.cn: 要求：加于人的规矩与为人设下的高标准，都是预期变成了压力。

branches.en: BARE GUESS: when evidence thins, the same verb softens into supposition.
branches.cn: 纯然猜测：证据变薄时，同一个动词软化为推测。

branches.en: WAITING FOR A BIRTH: the polite progressive borrows the waiting sense for pregnancy.
branches.cn: 等待生产：委婉的进行时把等待义借去指怀孕。

intro.en: Expect is a short Latin verb of two pieces, and both pieces build large English families.
intro.cn: expect 是一个由两部分构成的简短拉丁动词，两部分都构成大族英语词。

latinIntro.en: The prefix meaning 'out' gives export, exclude and extend; the looking root gives inspect, respect, spectator and spectacle.
latinIntro.cn: 表「向外」的前缀衍生 export、exclude 与 extend；表「看」的词根衍生 inspect、respect、spectator 与 spectacle。

items.example: The prefix aims the looking beyond the present place.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把目光投向当下所在之外。

items.example: The root supplies the watching that the word is built on.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供这个词所由建立的「看」。

items.example: The verb keeps the prefix and drops the repeated-looking suffix.
items.exampleCN: 动词保留前缀，去掉了表反复看的那层后缀。

items.example: The suffix builds the noun of the act.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出该行为的名词。

items.example: The noun is far more common than a literal translation suggests.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词远比字面直译看来常用。

items.example: The suffix builds the adjective for someone waiting.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出形容等待者的形容词。

items.meaning: waiting; about to become a parent
items.meaningCN: 期待着的；即将为人父母的
items.example: The adjective has a settled medical use.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词有固定的医疗用法。

items.example: The participle form builds the ordinary adjective of scheduled things.
items.exampleCN: 分词形式造出指按计划之事的常用形容词。

items.meaningCN: 按计划发生的；被预见的
items.example: The adjective appears in timetables and in test marking.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词出现在时刻表与阅卷语境中。

items.example: The negative prefix marks what no forecast covered.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀标出预判未覆盖之事。

definition_zh: 昂贵的；花钱多的；代价高的
definition_en: costing a lot of money or requiring much sacrifice
core_image: 钱包被掏空：买它的时候，钱像水一样流出去
scene: 橱窗里那双运动鞋标价高得惊人，男孩盯着看了很久，妈妈摇摇头说：These shoes are too expensive for our budget this month.
sceneCN: 这里 expensive 指「价格高、花钱多」（第 1 个义项：花费超出承受）；句意为这双鞋超出本月的预算。

derivatives.zh: 费用；开销（expensive 的名词根，义为「被花出去的钱」）
开支；经费（expense 复数，常指日常支出）
支出；花费（同源正式名词，义为「已付出的总额」）
花费；消耗（同源动词，义为「把钱付出去」）

senses.title: Costing a lot of money
senses.definition: having a price that is high or hard to pay
senses.definitionCN: 价格高到难以承受
senses.example: These shoes are too expensive for our budget this month.
senses.exampleCN: 这双鞋超出我们这个月的预算。
senses.why: The Latin root is to pay out: an expensive thing makes your money flow out of your pocket.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根是「付出」：昂贵的东西让钱从口袋里流出去。

senses.title: Costly in a non-monetary way
senses.definition: causing serious loss, harm, or sacrifice beyond money
senses.definitionCN: 带来金钱之外的严重损失或牺牲
senses.example: The delay proved expensive in reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误在声誉上代价惨重。
senses.why: When what flows out is not cash but trust or time, the paying-out image still holds.
senses.whyCN: 当流出去的不是现金而是信任或时间，「付出」的画面依然成立。

senses.title: Wasteful or extravagant in style
senses.definition: showing a habit of spending lavishly
senses.definitionCN: 显示出大手大脚的消费习惯
senses.example: He keeps an expensive lifestyle he cannot afford.
senses.exampleCN: 他维持着一种负担不起的奢侈生活方式。
senses.why: The person, not the price tag, is called expensive: money keeps flowing out by habit.
senses.whyCN: 被称为 expensive 的不是标价而是人：钱按习惯不断流出去。

senses.title: Requiring heavy upkeep or input
senses.definition: needing large ongoing spending to keep or operate
senses.definitionCN: 需要持续大笔投入才能维持
senses.example: This old machine is expensive to run.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧机器运营成本很高。
senses.why: The outflow never stops: even owning the thing keeps paying it out again and again.
senses.whyCN: 流出不会停止：光是拥有它，钱就要一次次再付出去。

intro.en: Expensive is the adjective of expense, rooted in Latin expendere, "to weigh out money to pay".
intro.cn: expensive 是 expense 的形容词，词根为拉丁语 expendere「称出钱来支付」。

items.en: Latin expendere meant "to weigh out, to pay out", from ex- (out) + pendere (to weigh, to hang).
items.cn: 拉丁语 expendere 意为「称出、付出」，由 ex-（向外）+ pendere（称量、悬挂）构成。

items.en: Pendere also gave pound, span, and pension: money measured and handed over.
items.cn: pendere 还衍生出 pound、span 与 pension：都是被称量后交出的东西。

items.en: Late Latin expendere narrowed to paying out money, the sense English borrowed.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语 expendere 收窄为「付出钱款」，英语借入的正是此义。

items.en: Middle English took expense and expensive from French in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪中古英语经法语借入 expense 与 expensive。

items.en: Modern English keeps the flow image: costly things make money pour out fast.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「流出」意象：昂贵的东西让钱快速流走。

note.en: These neighbours share the pend- root or the idea of high cost.
note.cn: 下列词与 expensive 同根，或同样有「代价高」的意思。

entries.definition: money that is spent
entries.definitionCN: 费用；开销（同根名词）

entries.definition: to spend or use up
entries.definitionCN: 花费；消耗（同根动词）

entries.definition: the total amount spent
entries.definitionCN: 支出总额（同根正式名词）

entries.definition: to become larger
entries.definitionCN: 扩张（拼写相近，词根为 pandere「展开」）

entries.definition: costing much; losing much
entries.definitionCN: 昂贵的；损失惨重的

entries.definition: informal for expensive

normal.en: Expense is the noun: at the expense of health.
normal.cn: expense 是名词：以健康为代价。

normal.en: Expand looks alike but means to grow wide — check the a!
normal.cn: expand 拼写相近但义为扩张——注意是字母 a。

normal.en: Spend is the everyday twin of the same root.

normal.en: Inexpensive flips it back: not costing much.

abstract.en: Picture a purse tipping over: coins pour out toward the shop counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个倾倒的钱包：硬币朝柜台流去。

abstract.en: Some costs are silent: reputation, time, and trust can pour out too.
abstract.cn: 有些代价是无声的：声誉、时间与信任同样会流走。

abstract.en: A scale hangs in the root: money weighed before it leaves.
abstract.cn: 词根里挂着一杆秤：钱在离开前先被称过。

examples.en: These shoes are too expensive for our budget this month.
examples.cn: 这双鞋超出我们这个月的预算。

examples.en: The delay proved expensive in reputation.
examples.cn: 这次延误在声誉上代价惨重。

examples.en: This old machine is expensive to run.

sensesIntro.en: From money weighed out of the purse, the word stretches to non-monetary loss, lavish habits, and heavy upkeep.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「从钱包称出钱」出发，扩展到非金钱损失、奢侈习惯与高昂维持成本。

definition_zh: 经验；经历；体验；感受（名词）；经历；体验（动词）
definition_en: knowledge or skill gained from doing something, an event that affects you, or the feeling it produces
core_image: 走过一遍的路留下脚印：事情发生后，它就存进了你这个人里
scene: 第一次独自坐火车去外婆家的孩子，下车时攥着车票回头看了看，妈妈说：This trip will be a valuable experience for you.
sceneCN: 这里 experience 指「一次有影响的经历」（第 2 个义项：亲历的事件）；句意为这次独自出行对你很有价值。

derivatives.zh: 有经验的；老练的（过去分词作形容词，义为「已被经历打磨过的」）
缺乏经验的（in- 加 experienced，义为「还没被事情打磨过」）
实验（同源近亲，义为「主动制造一次经历来试」）
经验主义的（同根异形，义为「以经历为依据的」）

senses.title: Knowledge gained by doing
senses.definition: the knowledge or skill that comes from actually doing or seeing something
senses.definitionCN: 从实际做或亲眼见中得来的知识与技能
senses.example: She has five years of teaching experience.
senses.exampleCN: 她有五年教学经验。
senses.why: The root is to try out through the body: what passes through you stays as know-how.
senses.whyCN: 词根是用身体去尝试：从你身上经过的东西会沉淀为本领。

senses.title: An event that happens to you
senses.definition: something that happens to you and leaves an effect
senses.definitionCN: 发生在你身上并留下影响的事
senses.example: This trip will be a valuable experience for you.
senses.exampleCN: 这次旅行对你将是一次宝贵的经历。
senses.why: The same passing-through, seen as one complete event rather than accumulated skill.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「经过」，这次被看作一个完整事件，而非积累的本领。

senses.title: The inner feeling of undergoing something
senses.definition: the conscious feeling produced by undergoing something
senses.definitionCN: 亲身经历某事时产生的内在感受
senses.example: Pain is a bitter experience no one enjoys.
senses.exampleCN: 疼痛是一种没人喜欢的痛苦体验。
senses.why: The path runs inside now: what passes through you is felt, not stored as skill.
senses.whyCN: 路线转入内在：经过你的是感受，而不是沉淀为技能的东西。

senses.title: To undergo or live through something
senses.definition: to meet with or live through something as it happens
senses.definitionCN: 在某事发生时遭遇或经受它
senses.example: The city experienced its worst storm in decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市经历了数十年来最严重的风暴。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: the person is now the road that events travel on.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词：人变成了事件驶过的那条路。

intro.en: Experience comes from Latin experiri, "to try out", through French, and keeps the sense of testing by living through it.
intro.cn: experience 源自拉丁语 experiri「尝试」，经法语进入英语，保留了「亲身经过来验证」的意思。

items.en: Latin experiri meant "to try, to test", from ex- (out of) + peritus (tested, skilled).
items.cn: 拉丁语 experiri 意为「尝试、检验」，由 ex-（从…出来）+ peritus（受试的、熟练的）构成。

items.en: The root per- carries the idea of risk: to try is to put yourself on the line.
items.cn: 词根 per- 带有「冒险」的意味：尝试就是把自己押上去。

items.en: Old French experience carried both the trying and the knowledge it yields.
items.cn: 古法语 experience 兼指尝试与尝试所得的知识。

items.en: Middle English borrowed it in the fourteenth century for tested knowledge and lived events.
items.cn: 十四世纪中古英语借入，兼指经过验证的知识与亲历的事件。

items.en: Modern English widened it to inner feeling and to the verb of undergoing events.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到内在感受，并用作「经历某事」的动词。

note.en: These neighbours share the per- root or the idea of living through something.
note.cn: 下列词与 experience 同根，或同样有「亲身经过」的意思。

normalIntro.en: Five associations from the real root and usage.
normalIntro.cn: 五条来自真实词根与用法的联想。

normal.en: ex- (out) + per- (try, risk): you send yourself out to be tested.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex-（向外）+ 词根 per-（尝试、冒险）：把自己派出去受试。

normal.en: Experiment is the same root making a test on purpose.
normal.cn: experiment 是同根词，故意制造一次测试。

normal.en: Expert is what testing makes of you.
normal.cn: expert 是被试炼打造出来的你。

normal.en: Experienced vs inexperienced: polished or not yet polished.
normal.cn: experienced 与 inexperienced：被打磨过与否。

normal.en: Learn from experience means the road itself was the teacher.
normal.cn: learn from experience 意思是这条路本身就是老师。

abstract.en: Picture footprints on a path: each event leaves a mark inside you.
abstract.cn: 想象路上的脚印：每件事都在你心里留下印记。

abstract.en: Skills are old footprints you can walk again; events are single big marks.
abstract.cn: 技能是可以重走的旧脚印，事件是一次性的大印记。

abstract.en: To experience is to be the road itself while events drive over.
abstract.cn: to experience 就是当事件驶过时，自己成为那条路。

examples.en: This trip will be a valuable experience for you.
examples.cn: 这次旅行对你将是一次宝贵的经历。

examples.en: She has five years of teaching experience.
examples.cn: 她有五年教学经验。

examples.en: The city experienced its worst storm in decades.
examples.cn: 这座城市经历了数十年来最严重的风暴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一颗死匹日恩死」——一颗死磕的匹夫每日经历磨炼，终成老手。

sensesIntro.en: From being tested by trying, the word covers gained skill, single events, inner feeling, and undergoing itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「尝试中受检验」出发，覆盖所得本领、单个事件、内在感受与「经历」这个动作。

core.cn: 核心意象：走过的路上留下的脚印

definition_zh: 实验；试验；尝试；做实验
definition_en: a test carried out under controlled conditions to discover or check something; also to carry out such a test, or to try something new
core_image: 两只同样的杯子并排放着，一只加了糖，一只没有，旁边一张纸上只写着一个待验证的问题
scene: 厨房桌上并排放着两只同样的杯子，一只加了糖，一只没加，旁边摊着一张写着待验证问题的纸。The student ran the experiment twice to see whether the sugar changed the result.
sceneCN: 这里 experiment 指「在受控条件下检验某个设想的实验」（第 1 个义项：受控的科学检验）；句意为这名学生把实验做了两遍，看加糖是否改变了结果。图中可辨识物件：两只杯子、糖罐、记录纸、铅笔。

pos.zh: 实验；试验；（新事物的）尝试

derivatives.zh: 实验的；试验性的
实验；试验过程
实验者
以实验方式；在实验上
经过试验的

senses.title: A controlled scientific test
senses.definition: a procedure carried out under controlled conditions in order to test a hypothesis or discover a fact
senses.definitionCN: 为检验假设或发现事实而在受控条件下进行的操作
senses.example: The student ran the experiment twice to see whether the sugar changed the result.
senses.exampleCN: 这名学生把实验做了两遍，看加糖是否改变了结果。
senses.why: The core sense is a deliberate trial in which conditions are arranged so that one factor can be watched.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是有意的试验：把条件安排好，好让某一个因素被观察。

senses.title: A tentative attempt
senses.definition: an attempt made without assurance of success, in order to learn what happens
senses.definitionCN: 在并无成功把握的情况下做出尝试，只为看看会怎样
senses.example: Her first attempt at repairing the radio was an experiment rather than a repair.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一次修收音机，更像一次试验，而不是一次修理。
senses.why: Outside science the word keeps the same shape without the controls: you try something because you do not yet know the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 在科学之外，这个词保留了同样的形态，只是没有受控条件：你因为还不知道结果而去试一试。

senses.title: A set exercise in a teaching lab
senses.titleCN: 课堂上按规程做的实验
senses.definition: a prescribed practical exercise that students perform to see a known result for themselves
senses.definitionCN: 学生按既定规程操作、亲眼看到已知结果的一种练习
senses.example: The class does the same experiment with vinegar and baking soda every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这个班每年秋天都做同一个醋与小苏打的实验。
senses.why: School labs repeat experiments whose answers are already known, so the word comes to mean the exercise rather than the inquiry.
senses.whyCN: 学校实验室重复的是答案已知的实验，于是这个词转而指那道练习，而非那次探究。

senses.title: A thought experiment
senses.definition: a scenario imagined in detail in order to test a principle that cannot be tried in reality
senses.definitionCN: 为检验无法在现实中操作的原理想象出来的详细情境
senses.example: Einstein's experiment with a falling elevator was carried out only in his head.
senses.exampleCN: 爱因斯坦那个关于下落电梯的实验只在头脑中进行。
senses.why: When the apparatus is imagination, the trial still keeps the name, because the point is still to test an idea.
senses.whyCN: 当器械换成想象时，这种试仍然沿用旧名，因为要点依旧是检验一个想法。

senses.title: An innovative departure
senses.titleCN: 在艺术或政策上的一次新尝试
senses.definition: a new way of doing something, tried in order to see whether it works better
senses.definitionCN: 为看清是否更好而尝试的一种新做法
senses.example: The theatre's experiment with a bare stage divided its critics.
senses.exampleCN: 这家剧院对空舞台的尝试使评论界分成两派。
senses.why: Any field that risks a new form borrows the word, since the new form is staked on an unknown outcome.
senses.whyCN: 任何冒险采用新形式的领域都会借用这个词，因为新形式押在一个未知的结果上。

senses.title: To carry out a scientific test
senses.definition: to perform a controlled test in order to gather evidence
senses.definitionCN: 为收集证据而进行受控检验
senses.example: They experimented on the alloy until they found its breaking point.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对这种合金反复做实验，直到找出它的断裂点。
senses.why: The verb is simply the activity named by the noun, turned into something one does.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词所指的活动，转成一个人去做的事情。

senses.title: To try something out
senses.definition: to try a substance, method or style in order to learn its effects
senses.definitionCN: 为弄清效果而试用某种物质、方法或风格
senses.example: He experimented with colder water and the tea stopped tasting bitter.
senses.exampleCN: 他试着用更冷的水，茶就不再发苦了。
senses.why: The verb broadens from the laboratory to any deliberate trial of a variable.
senses.whyCN: 动词从实验室扩展开来，指对某一变量做的任何有意的试用。

senses.title: A venture in one's own life
senses.titleCN: 人生中的一次尝试（抽象义）
senses.definition: used of a period or venture in which someone tries a different way of living or working
senses.definitionCN: 指某人尝试另一种生活或工作方式的一段时期或一项事业
senses.example: Moving to the coast was an experiment in living more slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 搬到海边，是一次把日子过慢些的尝试。
senses.why: The abstract sense treats a life choice as a trial whose result cannot be known in advance.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把人生选择当作一场结果无法预知的试验。

intro.en: Experiment goes back to Latin experiri 'to try, test', whose noun experimentum meant 'a trial, a proof'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词可追溯到拉丁语 experiri「尝试、检验」，其名词 experimentum 意为「试、证明」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Periri meant 'to try, to attempt', and from the same stock came periculum 'trial, danger' and peritus 'experienced'. The link among them is generally accepted.
items.cn: periri 意为「尝试、试探」，同一词干还生出 periculum「试、危险」与 peritus「有经验的」。三者之间的关联一般认为是可靠的。

items.en: The prefix ex- 'out' added to periri gave experiri 'to try out, to test thoroughly', with the sense of carrying a trial through to its end.
items.cn: 前缀 ex-「向外」加 periri 构成 experiri「试出来、彻底检验」，带有把试验做到尽头的意思。

items.en: The noun experimentum named a trial, a proof or a piece of evidence, and also the experience gained from trying.
items.cn: 名词 experimentum 指一次试验、一项证明或一份证据，也指由尝试得来的经验。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century through French, at first with the older sense of experience or observation rather than a staged procedure.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪经法语吸收这个词，最初取的是「经验、观察」的旧义，而非安排好的操作步骤。

items.en: From the seventeenth century, with the rise of organised investigation, the word settled into its present meaning of a controlled test of a hypothesis.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，随着有组织的探究兴起，这个词固定为今天「对假设作受控检验」的意思。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin form): the root behind periri is reconstructed, and though the family with peril and expert is widely accepted, no attested earlier form can be quoted.
items.cn: 来源不确定（拉丁语之前的形态）：periri 背后的词根属重构形式；尽管它与表示危险、有经验的同族关系被广泛接受，却没有可引用的更早实证形式。

note.en: Group one separates the near relatives built on the same Latin root; group two separates the ordinary words for a test.
note.cn: 第一组辨析同出拉丁词根的近亲；第二组辨析表示「检验」的常用词。

entries.definition: Built on the same verb for trying, but it means what one has lived through, not a staged test.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个表示尝试的动词，但指亲身经历过的事，而非安排好的检验。

entries.definition: From the adjective for 'experienced', so an expert is one who has tried things and learned; it names a person, not a procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 来自表示「有经验的」形容词，因此指试过并学到东西的人；它指人，不指程序。

entries.definition: From the noun for a trial that puts one at risk, so it survives only as the word for serious danger.
entries.definitionCN: 来自表示带风险的试的名词，因此只留下「严重危险」这一义。

entries.definition: The doer of an experiment; the difference from the noun is only the agent suffix, which is easy to miss in fast reading.
entries.definitionCN: 指做实验的人；与名词的差别只在表示施动者的后缀，快速阅读时容易看漏。

entries.definition: The general word for checking whether something works or is true; an experiment is its formal, scientific counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指检查某物是否有效或属实的词；experiment 是它正式、科学化的对应词。

entries.definition: A trial is a first use or run to see how something performs, often of a product or a method already made.
entries.definitionCN: 指为看某物表现如何而作的首次使用或试运行，多用于已经做成的产品或方法。

entries.definition: A study is a planned investigation, often longer and observational; not every study manipulates conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 指有计划的调查，通常更长且偏观察；并非每项研究都操纵条件。

entries.definition: To probe is to investigate something hidden or unclear, often with repeated small inquiries rather than one designed trial.
entries.definitionCN: 指追查隐藏或不明之事，常用反复的小探询，而非一次设计好的试验。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is built from a Latin verb for trying plus a prefix meaning 'out', so it is a trying-out to the end.
normal.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示「尝试」的动词加一个意为「向外」的前缀构成，因此是「试到底」。

normal.en: The same root gives peril and expert: a trial is risky, and one who has come through trials is experienced.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出「危险」与「有经验的」：试是有风险的，闯过许多试的人便有经验。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the method: carry out an experiment, a controlled experiment, experiment with a new method.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出方法：进行实验、对照实验、尝试新方法。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one form, so the thing and the doing are the same word.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，因此这件事与做这件事是同一个词。

normal.en: A thought experiment keeps the name even when the apparatus is only imagination.
normal.cn: 思想实验即使器械只是想象，也仍沿用这个名字。

abstract.en: Picture two identical cups on a table, differing in exactly one spoonful.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上两只一模一样的杯子，只差一勺东西。

abstract.en: Picture a lock with many keys, tried one at a time while someone writes down each result.
abstract.cn: 想象一把锁与许多钥匙，一把一把地试，旁边有人记下每次结果。

abstract.en: Picture a life lived for one year as a question rather than an answer.
abstract.cn: 想象把一年生活当作一个问题来过，而不是当作一个答案。

examples.en: The experiment showed that the plants grew faster in weak light.
examples.cn: 实验显示这些植物在弱光下长得更快。

examples.en: She experimented with three glazes before choosing one.
examples.cn: 她试了三种釉料才选定一种。

examples.en: No experiment on human subjects was allowed without consent.
examples.cn: 未经同意不得在人类受试者身上做实验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「试到底」：前缀表示向外，词根表示尝试，把一件事一直试到见结果 → 实验、尝试

root: 拉丁 experiri「尝试、检验」= ex-「向外」+ periri「试」；同族有 periculum「危险」与 peritus「有经验的」；experiri 的拉丁语之前形态属重构形式，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture, a deliberate trial: first the controlled test, then any tentative attempt, a classroom exercise, a trial run only in the mind, a new departure, the act of testing, trying a variable, and finally a life tried as an experiment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开，即有意的一次试：先是在受控条件下的检验，接着是任何试探性的尝试、课堂练习、只在头脑中进行的试、一种新做法、做实验这一行为、试用某个变量，最后把人生本身当作一次试验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two identical cups differing by one spoonful, and a written question waiting for an answer.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只只差一勺的相同杯子，以及一个等着答案的书面问题。

branches.en: The designed trial and the act of running it: the noun and the verb name one operation.
branches.cn: 设计好的试与执行这次试：名词与动词指同一操作。

branches.en: The loose attempt: trying something without guarantees, whether a repair or a colder cup of tea.
branches.cn: 宽松的试：在没有保证的情况下试，无论是修东西还是换冷水泡茶。

branches.en: The exercise and the imagined run: both repeat a known or imagined procedure for the sake of seeing.
branches.cn: 练习与想象中的试：两者都为「看见」而重演一个已知或设想的过程。

branches.en: The departure: a new form staked on an unknown outcome, in theatre or in policy.
branches.cn: 新做法：把新形式押在未知结果上，无论在剧场还是在政策上。

branches.en: The life trial: a year lived as a question rather than an answer.
branches.cn: 人生的试：把一年当作问题而非答案来过。

intro.en: Experiment is a Latin verb-noun pair in which a prefix, a root and a suffix each carry part of the meaning, and the same pieces build its English family.
intro.cn: 这个词是一组拉丁动词与名词，前缀、词根与后缀各担一部分意义，同样的部件也构成它的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin periri and its noun periculum supply the root; ex- adds the sense of carrying a trial through, and -mentum names the result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「试」的动词与其名词提供词根；前缀增添「把试做到底」的意思，后缀则命名结果。

items.example: The prefix makes the trying exhaustive rather than casual.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使「试」成为彻底的，而非随意的。

items.example: The root carries the whole idea of a trial.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载「试」的全部意思。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into the record or result of a trial.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词转为一次试的记录或结果。

items.example: The compound verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个合成动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The Latin noun already joins the act and its evidence.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词已把行为与其证据合在一起。

items.example: English keeps one form for the thing and the doing.
items.exampleCN: 英语用同一个形式兼指这件事与做这件事。

items.example: The adjective marks whatever belongs to the testing stage.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记属于试验阶段的一切。

items.example: The noun names the practice rather than one trial.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指实践，而非某一次试。

items.example: The agent suffix names the person running the trial.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀指执行这次试的人。

definition_en: a person with deep knowledge or skill in a field, or having such knowledge and skill

scene: 法庭上，证人席旁摆着几张影像片和骨骼示意图。 The expert told the court that the crack had been caused by the fall.
sceneCN: 这里 expert 是「专家证人」（第 3 个义项：在法庭上提供专业意见的专家）；句意：这位专家在法庭上说，裂痕是摔倒造成的。

senses.title: A person who knows a field deeply
senses.titleCN: 专家：把某个领域摸透的人
senses.definition: a person with a high level of knowledge or skill in a particular subject
senses.definitionCN: 在某一学科或领域拥有高水平知识或技能的人
senses.example: She is a leading expert on marine mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 她是海洋哺乳动物方面的顶尖专家。
senses.why: Latin expertus means 'tried, tested'. An expert is not someone who has merely read about a field but someone whose knowledge has been tested by the work itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 expertus 意为“试过的、验过的”。专家不是只在书上读过某个领域的人，而是其知识被实际工作检验过的人。

senses.title: A specialist called in to advise
senses.titleCN: 顾问专家：被请来出主意的人
senses.definition: a specialist whose advice is sought on a practical problem
senses.definitionCN: 就实际问题被请来提供建议的专门人才
senses.example: The company hired an expert to review its security.
senses.exampleCN: 公司请了一位专家来审查安保。
senses.why: The tested knowledge becomes useful to others. A person who has already walked the ground is called in so that others do not have to repeat every trial.
senses.whyCN: 被检验过的知识对别人有了用处。已经走过这条路的人被请进来，别人就不必把每一次试验都重做一遍。

senses.title: Expert witness in court
senses.titleCN: 专家证人：在法庭上提供专业判断
senses.definition: a witness allowed to give an opinion based on special knowledge rather than on what was directly seen
senses.definitionCN: 获准依据专门知识、而非亲眼所见来提供意见的证人
senses.example: The expert testified that the crack came from a fall.
senses.exampleCN: 这位专家作证说，裂痕是摔倒造成的。
senses.why: The legal sense is recorded from 1825. The courtroom needs knowledge that no ordinary witness could supply, so the tested person is placed in the witness box.
senses.whyCN: 这一法律义记录于 1825 年。法庭需要普通证人无法提供的知识，于是把“被检验过的人”放进了证人席。

senses.title: Skilled through long practice
senses.definition: adjective: highly skilled or experienced in doing something
senses.definitionCN: 形容词：做某事极为熟练或经验丰富
senses.example: He is an expert driver.
senses.exampleCN: 他是一位熟练的司机。
senses.why: The same past participle becomes an adjective: hands that have done the task many times are expert hands, whether or not the person is called an expert.
senses.whyCN: 同一个过去分词又变成形容词：反复做过这件事的手就是 expert hands，不管这个人是否被称为专家。

senses.title: Based on special knowledge
senses.titleCN: 专家的：依据专门知识作出的
senses.definition: adjective: coming from or based on specialized knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 形容词：来自专门知识或以其为依据的
senses.example: He gave expert advice on restoring the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 他就修复屋顶给出了专家建议。
senses.why: Advice is expert when it carries the weight of trials the listener has not run. The adjective marks the source of the knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 建议之所以是 expert，是因为它承载着听者没有做过的那些试验。形容词标记的是知识的来源。

senses.title: Done with mastery: an expert performance
senses.titleCN: 精湛的：做得像行家一样
senses.definition: adjective: done with great skill and control, especially in art, sport, or surgery
senses.definitionCN: 形容词：以极高技能与控制力完成，尤指艺术、运动或手术
senses.example: She gave an expert performance despite the pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管压力很大，她的表演依然精湛。
senses.why: The noun's 'tested person' becomes a quality of the action itself. A performance is expert when it looks as if trained hands are guiding every move.
senses.whyCN: 名词“被检验过的人”变成了动作本身的品质。当每一个动作都像由训练有素的手在引导时，表演就是 expert。

senses.title: Expert system: knowledge in a machine
senses.titleCN: 专家系统：装进机器里的专业知识
senses.definition: adjective, technical: designating a computer program that reproduces the decisions of a human specialist
senses.definitionCN: 形容词技术用法：指能重现人类专家判断的计算机程序
senses.example: The clinic uses an expert system to flag drug interactions.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所使用专家系统来标记药物相互作用。
senses.why: The knowledge of the tested specialist is written into rules. The machine inherits the adjective, though it has never tried anything itself.
senses.whyCN: 被检验过的专家的知识被写成规则。机器继承了形容词，尽管它自己从未“试”过任何事。

senses.title: Expert in, on, at: the fixed patterns
senses.titleCN: 固定搭配：expert in / on / at
senses.definition: in fixed phrases, expert in or on a field, and expert at doing something
senses.definitionCN: 固定短语中，expert in/on 接领域，expert at 接做某事
senses.example: She is expert at avoiding direct questions.
senses.exampleCN: 她很擅长回避直接提问。
senses.why: The preposition shows where the tested skill sits: in a subject, on a topic, at a performance. The adjective keeps the same 'proved by practice' core.
senses.whyCN: 介词显示被检验的技能落在哪里：in 接学科，on 接话题，at 接具体表现。形容词仍保留“经实践验证”的内核。

intro.en: Expert comes from Latin expertus, the past participle of experiri 'to try, test'. The adjective arrived first, in the late 14th century, meaning 'taught by experience'; the person-noun followed in the early 15th century.
intro.cn: expert 来自拉丁语 expertus，即 experiri“尝试、检验”的过去分词。形容词先到，14 世纪晚期意为“由经验教会的”；指人的名词随后于 15 世纪早期出现。

items.en: Experiri meant 'to try, test'. Its past participle expertus meant 'tried, tested, experienced', and peritus meant 'experienced, skilled'.
items.cn: experiri 意为“尝试、检验”。其过去分词 expertus 意为“试过的、验过的、有经验的”，peritus 意为“有经验的、熟练的”。

items.en: The root is traced to PIE *per- 'to try, risk'. The idea of danger and trial is built into the word: knowledge comes from attempts that could fail.
items.cn: 词根可追溯到原始印欧语 *per-“试、冒险”。危险与试炼的观念就嵌在词里：知识来自可能失败的尝试。

items.en: The English adjective is first recorded as 'experienced, taught by experience, skilled'. It describes a person or a hand that has been tested.
items.cn: 英语形容词最早记录为“有经验的、由经验教会的、熟练的”。它描述一个被检验过的人或一双被检验过的手。

items.en: The noun appears as 'a person wise through experience'. The adjective's tested quality is now attached to a person who can be consulted.
items.cn: 名词出现，意为“靠经验而明智的人”。形容词的“被检验”品质，现在附着在一个可以被请教的人身上。

items.en: The legal phrase expert witness is recorded in 1825: a witness selected for professional knowledge rather than for direct observation.
items.cn: 法律短语 expert witness 记录于 1825 年：证人因专业知识而非亲眼观察被选中。

items.en: Expertise, the noun for the knowledge itself, is borrowed from French in 1868. English keeps expert for the person or the adjective and expertise for the body of knowledge.
items.cn: 指知识本身的名词 expertise 于 1868 年借自法语。英语用 expert 指人或作形容词，用 expertise 指那一整套知识。

note.en: The first group shares spelling or word parts with expert; the second group shares meaning. Form first, then sense.
note.cn: 第一组与 expert 共享拼写或构词成分；第二组共享词义。先看词形，再看词义。

entries.definition: the knowledge and skill of an expert. Expert is the person or the adjective; expertise is the body of knowledge itself.
entries.definitionCN: 专家的知识与技能。expert 指人或作形容词；expertise 指那一整套知识本身。

entries.definition: a test carried out to find out something. It shares experiri 'to try'; an expert is a person shaped by many such tests.
entries.definitionCN: 为查明某事而做的实验。它共享 experiri“尝试”；专家则是被许多次这样的尝试塑造出来的人。

entries.definition: to carry goods out of a country. It is ex- + portare 'to carry', not periri 'to try'.
entries.definitionCN: 把货物运出国外。它是 ex- + portare“运送”，不是 periri“尝试”。

entries.definition: a person who concentrates on one branch of a subject, often medicine. Specialist stresses the narrow field; expert stresses the tested level of knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 专注于某一分支（常指医学）的人。specialist 强调领域窄；expert 强调知识经过检验、水平高。

entries.definition: a person or work recognized as a source of reliable knowledge. Authority adds public recognition; expert adds tested skill.
entries.definitionCN: 被公认为可靠知识来源的人或著作。authority 多了公众认可；expert 多了被检验的技能。

entries.definition: a person who works in a skilled occupation. Professional stresses paid status and standards; an expert may be unpaid.
entries.definitionCN: 从事专业技能职业的人。professional 强调受薪身份与行业标准；expert 不一定以此为业。

entries.definition: a person with expert judgment in art, food, or wine. Connoisseur is about cultivated taste; expert is broader and can be technical.
entries.definitionCN: 在艺术、食物或酒方面有专家判断力的人。connoisseur 强调培养出的品味；expert 范围更广，可以是技术性的。

normalIntro.en: Real parts, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 真实的构词成分、真实短语和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Experiri 'to try, test' is the core: an expert is a person whose knowledge has been tested by the work.
normal.cn: experiri“尝试、检验”是核心：专家就是知识被工作检验过的人。

normal.en: Expertus is the past participle 'tried, proved'. The adjective came first in the late 14th century; the person-noun followed in the early 15th.
normal.cn: expertus 是过去分词“试过的、验过的”。形容词在 14 世纪晚期先出现，指人的名词在 15 世纪早期跟上。

normal.en: Expertise is the noun for the knowledge, borrowed from French in 1868. Expert is the person or adjective; expertise is the body of knowledge.
normal.cn: expertise 是指知识的名词，1868 年借自法语。expert 指人或作形容词；expertise 指那一整套知识。

normal.en: Expert witness became a legal term in 1825: a witness chosen for knowledge rather than for what he or she saw.
normal.cn: expert witness 于 1825 年成为法律术语：证人因知识而非亲眼所见被选中。

normal.en: Do not confuse expert with export: export is ex- + portare 'carry', so it means carry goods out, not tested knowledge.
normal.cn: 不要把 expert 和 export 混淆：export 是 ex- + portare“运送”，意为把货物运出去，不是被检验的知识。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of hands that have repeated one task thousands of times. The knowledge is in the calluses before it is in any certificate.
abstract.cn: 想象一双把同一件事重复了上千次的手。知识先长在茧里，然后才写进证书。

abstract.en: A person is not an expert because of a title, but because a test has left a mark. Expertus means proved, not merely trained.
abstract.cn: 一个人成为专家，不是因为头衔，而是因为检验留下了痕迹。expertus 意为“被验证过的”，不只是“被训练过的”。

abstract.en: The expert stands at the edge of ordinary knowledge and is called in when the usual route runs out.
abstract.cn: 专家站在日常知识的边缘；当常规路径走不通时，人们就把他请进来。

examples.en: She is a leading expert on marine mammals.
examples.cn: 她是海洋哺乳动物方面的顶尖专家。

examples.en: The court heard expert testimony on the bullet's path.
examples.cn: 法庭听取了关于子弹轨迹的专家证词。

examples.en: He gave expert advice on restoring the roof.
examples.cn: 他就修复屋顶给出了专家建议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱克死破特」——把难题“破”到底、试到头的人 → expert 专家、熟练的

root: 源自拉丁语 expertus「试过的、验过的」，是 experiri「尝试、检验」的过去分词，词根 per- 含“试、冒险”之意。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of expert, all built on one idea: knowledge proved by trial. The proved person can be consulted, can testify, can guide a hand, or can be written into a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: expert 的八个义项都建立在一个观念上：知识经过试炼而被证明。被证明的人可以被请教、可以作证、可以引导一双手，也可以被写进机器里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands that have tried the same task until the knowledge is proved.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手把同一件事试到知识被证明为止。

branches.en: a person trusted for deep knowledge
branches.cn: 因深厚知识而被信任的人

branches.en: the specialist brought into court
branches.cn: 被请进法庭的专家

branches.en: the adjective of trained skill
branches.cn: 形容练出来的本事

branches.en: work done like a master
branches.cn: 做得像行家一样

branches.en: machine systems and set phrases
branches.cn: 专家系统与固定搭配

intro.en: Expert is formed from ex- 'out' and the per- stem of experiri 'to try'. English builds expertise, expertly and expertness directly on the finished word.
intro.cn: expert 由 ex-“出”和 experiri“尝试”的 per- 词干构成。英语直接在成品词上构成 expertise、expertly、expertness。

latinIntro.en: Latin experiri 'to try, test' gives the participle expertus and the noun experientia; peritus 'experienced, tested' shares the same root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 experiri“尝试、检验”生出分词 expertus 和名词 experientia；peritus“有经验的、经过检验的”共享同一词根。

items.meaning: a person proved by experience; skilled
items.meaningCN: 经经验证明的人；熟练的（ex- 出 + peritus 经过检验的）
items.example: They consulted an expert on soil.
items.exampleCN: 他们请教了一位土壤专家。

items.structure: expert + -ise (French noun of quality or skill)
items.meaning: the knowledge or skill of an expert
items.meaningCN: 专业知识；专长（-ise 构成性质名词，1868 年借自法语）
items.exampleCN: 这份工作需要技术专长。

items.meaningCN: 熟练地；内行地（-ly 构成副词）
熟练；精通（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The expertness of her stitching was obvious.
items.exampleCN: 她缝线的熟练程度一目了然。

items.meaning: a trial carried out to learn something
items.meaningCN: 实验；试验（尝试 + 名词后缀）

items.meaning: knowledge or skill gained by doing
items.meaningCN: 经验；经历（由“尝试”得来的知识）
items.example: She has ten years of experience.

items.meaning: based on experience rather than theory
items.meaningCN: 经验的；体验式的（-ial 构成形容词）
无经验的；不老练的（in- 表否定 + 分词形容词）
items.example: He was too inexperienced for the role.
items.exampleCN: 对这个角色来说，他太没经验了。

definition_zh: 解释；说明；讲解；阐明原因
definition_en: to make something clear or easy to understand by giving details or reasons
core_image: 把一团乱麻摊开在桌上：一根一根理顺，直到谁都能看清纹路
scene: 弟弟看不懂棋盘上为什么输，哥哥把每一步摆回原位，指着棋子说：Let me explain why your knight lost the game.
sceneCN: 这里 explain 指「把道理讲清楚」（第 1 个义项：说明使易于理解）；句意为哥哥解释输棋的原因。

collocations.zh: 为自己的言行说明理由

senses.title: To make something easy to understand
senses.definition: to give details or reasons so that something becomes clear
senses.definitionCN: 通过给出细节或原因，使某事变得清楚易懂
senses.example: Let me explain why your knight lost the game.
senses.exampleCN: 让我来解释为什么你的马输了这局棋。
senses.why: The Latin root is to flatten out: a tangled thing is spread open level, so its folds show plainly.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根是「摊平」：把一团乱的东西摊平展开，褶皱就看得清清楚楚。

senses.title: To give reasons for one's behaviour
senses.titleCN: 为自己的言行说明理由
senses.definition: to tell why you did or said something
senses.definitionCN: 说出你为何这么做、这么说
senses.example: He was asked to explain his absence at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他被要求说明为什么没来开会。
senses.why: The spreading act turns inward: now your own conduct is the tangle laid flat.
senses.whyCN: 摊开的动作转向自身：这次被摊平的是你自己的行为。

senses.title: To be the reason behind something
senses.definition: to be the cause that makes something happen or make sense
senses.definitionCN: 作为让某事发生或说得通的缘由
senses.example: Her long silence explains the sudden change.
senses.exampleCN: 她的长期沉默解释了这场突然的转变。
senses.why: Once the knot is spread open, its shape alone shows why the thread ran as it did.
senses.whyCN: 乱麻摊开后，它的形状本身就说明了线为何这样走。

senses.title: To give reasons for something unfortunate
senses.definition: to make clear why something bad happened, often to excuse it
senses.definitionCN: 说明坏事为何发生，常带开脱意味
senses.example: Nothing can explain the loss except pure bad luck.
senses.exampleCN: 除了运气太差，这场失利没有别的缘由。
senses.why: The same opening-up applied to failure: laying the accident flat to see what bent it.
senses.whyCN: 同样的展开用在失败上：把事故摊平，看清是哪里折了。

intro.en: Explain comes from Latin explanare, "to make level, to flatten out", a root image of spreading things flat.
intro.cn: explain 源自拉丁语 explanare「弄平、摊开」，词根画面是把东西摊平展开。

items.en: Latin explanare meant "to flatten, to make level", from ex- (out) + planus (flat, level).
items.cn: 拉丁语 explanare 意为「弄平、摊平」，由 ex-（向外）+ planus（平的）构成。

items.en: The plain in explain is the same word family as plane and plan: something spread out evenly.
items.cn: explain 里的 plain 与 plane、plan 同族：都是被均匀摊开的东西。

items.en: Confusion with the similar plain gave the spelling its extra i in English.
items.cn: 与 plain 的混淆让英语拼写里多了一个 i。

items.en: Middle English took explain and explanen from Latin in the fifteenth century, meaning to make clear.
items.cn: 十五世纪中古英语从拉丁语借入，义为「讲清楚」。

items.en: Modern English settled the spelling explain and kept the flat-image in phrases like explain away.
items.cn: 现代英语定形为 explain，摊平意象保留在 explain away 等短语中。

note.en: These neighbours share the planus root or the act of making things clear.
note.cn: 下列词与 explain 同根，或同样有「讲清楚」的动作。

entries.definition: level, clear, simple

entries.definition: a drawing spread out on a surface

entries.definition: to unfold in detail

entries.definition: to explain the cause of

normalIntro.en: Five associations from the real root and usage.
normalIntro.cn: 五条来自真实词根与用法的联想。

normal.en: ex- (out) + plain (flat): spread the tangle flat to see it.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex-（向外）+ plain（平）：把乱团摊平才看得清。

normal.en: Plain is the family word: a plain statement needs no more explaining.
normal.cn: plain 是同族词：平实的陈述无需再多解释。

normal.en: Explanation is the noun: write your explanation on paper.
normal.cn: explanation 是名词：把解释写在纸上。

normal.en: Explain away means to flatten a fault until it looks small.
normal.cn: explain away 是把错误摊平到看起来很小。

normal.en: Explicable things can be spread open; inexplicable ones cannot.
normal.cn: explicable 能被摊开，inexplicable 摊不开。

abstract.en: Picture a knotted rope laid out on a table, straightened thread by thread.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上一根打了结的绳，被一寸寸理直。

abstract.en: A good explanation is a map: folded land becomes flat paper.
abstract.cn: 好的解释是一张地图：起伏的大地摊平成纸。

abstract.en: When you explain yourself, the knot on the table is your own behaviour.
abstract.cn: 当你 explain yourself，桌上那团乱麻就是你的行为。

examples.en: Let me explain why your knight lost the game.
examples.cn: 让我来解释为什么你的马输了这局棋。

examples.en: He was asked to explain his absence at the meeting.
examples.cn: 他被要求说明为什么没来开会。

examples.cn: 她的长期沉默解释了这场突然的转变。

sensesIntro.en: From flattening a knot into view, the word covers teaching, self-justification, and causes laid bare.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「把结摊平给人看」出发，覆盖讲解、自我辩解与摆明缘由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tangle spread out flat on a table
core.cn: 核心意象：乱麻被摊平在桌上

branches.en: the tangle opened so a learner can see
branches.cn: 乱团被摊开给学习者看

branches.en: one's own conduct as the opened knot
branches.cn: 被摊开的是自己的行为

branches.en: the opened shape itself shows the cause
branches.cn: 摊开的形状本身显出缘由

branches.en: failure laid flat to find the bend
branches.cn: 把失败摊平找折点

branches.en: making clear and giving reasons are one act
branches.cn: 讲清楚与给原因是一体

intro.cn: 词族立足于 planus（平），加向外前缀 ex-。

latinIntro.en: Latin cousins from the planus root.
latinIntro.cn: planus 词根的拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 表达；表示；榨出；特快的；快递；明确的
definition_en: to say or show what you think or feel, or to press liquid out of something
core_image: 手一压，汁水从果子里出来，话从心里出来，两件事是同一个动作
scene: 早餐店里，店主把刚榨好的橙汁递给客人，说：We express the oranges fresh every morning.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「榨出、压出汁液」（第 3 个义项：用压力把汁液挤出）；句意为这家店每天早上现榨橙子。

derivatives.zh: 表达；表情；词语
富于表现力的
明确地；特意地
表现力
面无表情的

senses.title: Say what one thinks or feels
senses.titleCN: 说出自己的想法或感受
senses.definition: to put thoughts or feelings into words
senses.definitionCN: 把想法或感受用词语说出来
senses.example: He expressed his doubts politely but clearly.
senses.exampleCN: 他有礼而清楚地表达了自己的疑虑。
senses.why: The oldest image is pressing something out, and a thought pressed out through the mouth becomes speech.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象是把东西压出来，而想法从嘴里被压出就成了言语。

senses.title: Show feeling through art or action
senses.titleCN: 通过艺术或行为表现情感
senses.definition: to show a feeling or idea through a work, gesture or act rather than a statement
senses.definitionCN: 通过作品、姿态或行为而不是陈述来显示情感或观点
senses.example: The mural expresses the community's grief.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅壁画表达了社区的悲伤。
senses.why: The channel need not be words; anything that lets an inner state come out can carry the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 渠道不必是词语；任何能让内在状态出来的东西都能承载同一个动词。

senses.title: Press juice or oil out
senses.definition: to squeeze liquid out of fruit, seeds or peel by pressure
senses.definitionCN: 用压力从果实、种子或果皮中挤出液体
senses.example: The press expresses oil from the seeds.
senses.exampleCN: 压榨机从种子里榨出油。
senses.why: This is the literal root meaning, still alive in food processing and perfumery.
senses.whyCN: 这是词根的字面意义，在食品加工与香料制作中仍然活着。

senses.title: A fast train
senses.definition: a train that makes few stops and travels quickly
senses.definitionCN: 停站少、运行速度快的列车
senses.example: They caught the night express to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搭上了开往海岸的夜间特快。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century railways borrowed the word to mean a service that presses straight through without delays.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的铁路借用这个词，指一路直推、不作耽搁的服务。

senses.title: Fast delivery service
senses.definition: a service that sends letters or parcels quickly and directly
senses.definitionCN: 快速直接地寄送信件或包裹的服务
senses.example: The package went by express and arrived next morning.
senses.exampleCN: 包裹走快递，第二天早上就到了。
senses.why: The same idea of direct speed moved from trains to mail and parcels.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「直达速度」从列车移到了邮件与包裹。

senses.title: Clearly stated and deliberate
senses.titleCN: 明确说出的；特意如此的
senses.definition: stated openly and with a clear purpose, rather than implied
senses.definitionCN: 公开说明且目的清楚，而非暗示的
senses.example: She came with the express purpose of resigning.
senses.exampleCN: 她来的明确目的就是辞职。
senses.why: Something expressly set out is pressed into clear view, so the adjective came to mean explicit.
senses.whyCN: 被明确摆出来的东西是被压进清晰视野的，因此这个形容词引申为「明确的」。

senses.title: Represent by symbols
senses.definition: to represent a value, relation or idea in symbols or a formula
senses.definitionCN: 用符号或公式表示一个值、关系或观点
senses.example: Express the ratio as a fraction in lowest terms.
senses.exampleCN: 把这个比表示成最简分数。
senses.why: Mathematics presses an abstract relation into visible symbols, continuing the same outward movement.
senses.whyCN: 数学把抽象关系压进可见符号，延续同一个向外的动作。

senses.title: Cause a gene to produce a product
senses.definition: in biology, to make the information in a gene produce a working molecule
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学中，使基因中的信息产生可用的分子
senses.example: These cells express the protein at high levels.
senses.exampleCN: 这些细胞高水平地表达这种蛋白质。
senses.why: A gene's instructions are pressed out into the cell as a product, which is why the same verb serves biology.
senses.whyCN: 基因的指令被压出到细胞里成为产物，因此同一个动词也服务于生物学。

intro.en: Express comes through Old French from Latin exprimere 'to press out, represent', built on ex- 'out' and premere 'to press'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: express 经古法语来自拉丁语 exprimere「压出、表现」，由拉丁语表示「向外」的前缀与 premere「压」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Premere 'to press' is the physical core. Its deeper origin is not established, and the root form often proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: premere「压」是物理核心。其更深来源未得到证明，常为它提出的词根形式属于重构。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus premere gave exprimere 'to squeeze out'; the verb then acquired the mental sense 'to represent, portray, utter'.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的拉丁前缀加 premere 得到 exprimere「挤出」；这个动词随后获得「表现、描绘、说出」的心理意义。

items.en: Old French espresser and expresser carried the verb into English in the fourteenth century with both the physical and the representational senses.
items.cn: 古法语 espresser 与 expresser 在十四世纪把这个动词带入英语，同时带有物理义与表现义。

items.en: From the seventeenth century a special messenger or dispatch was called an express; railways extended the label to fast trains in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，专门的信使或急件被称为 express；铁路在十九世纪把这个标签扩展到快车。

items.en: The adjective meaning 'clearly stated' developed in the sixteenth century from the idea of something expressly set out.
items.cn: 表示「明确说出」的形容词义在十六世纪发展出来，来自「被特意摆出来」的想法。

items.en: Source uncertain: exact dates of the railway and mail senses vary by region, and the pre-Latin origin of premere remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：铁路义与邮件义的确切年代因地区而异，premere 在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the same or neighbouring roots; group two holds near synonyms for the core act of saying or showing.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词根或邻近词根的外形相近词；第二组是「说」与「显示」这一核心动作的近义词。

entries.definition: Italian borrowed the same Latin verb for coffee pressed out under steam, so the coffee and the English verb share a root.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利语借用了同一个拉丁动词，指用蒸汽压出的咖啡，因此这种咖啡与英语动词同根。

entries.definition: With 'in' rather than 'out': to press a mark or feeling into someone's mind rather than to bring something out.
entries.definitionCN: 用的是「向内」而非「向外」的前缀：把印记或感受压进某人心里，而不是把东西带出来。

entries.definition: It looks like a sibling, but its root means 'to drive', not 'to press'; it means to force someone or something out.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像同族词，其实词根意为「驱赶」而非「压」；意思是把某人或某物赶出去。

entries.definition: It shares the 'out' prefix but its root means 'to draw or pull'; extraction pulls something out rather than pressing it.
entries.definitionCN: 同样带「向外」前缀，但词根意为「拉、抽」；提取是拉出某物，而不是压出。

entries.definition: To carry an idea across to someone; it stresses successful transfer, while express stresses the outward act.
entries.definitionCN: 把想法传递给别人；强调成功送达，而 express 强调向外的动作。

entries.definition: To say something clearly and formally; express is broader and can cover art, gestures and formulas.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而正式地说出；express 更宽，可涵盖艺术、姿态与公式。

entries.definition: A formal verb for producing sounds or words; it has no physical squeezing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指发出声音或词语的正式动词；没有物理上的挤压义。

entries.definition: To express an idea clearly and in an organized way; it adds the idea of clear structure.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而有条理地表达想法；多出「结构清晰」这一层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the pressing image, the prefix contrast, the transport sense and the family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：压出意象、前缀对比、交通义与同族词。

normal.en: The root means 'press out': juice is expressed from fruit, words from a mind.
normal.cn: 词根意为「压出」：从果子里压出汁，从心里压出话。

normal.en: Prefix contrast: outward pressing is express, inward pressing is impress.
normal.cn: 前缀对比：向外压是「表达」，向内压是「给人印象」。

normal.en: Transport pair: an express train and express mail both move directly and quickly.
normal.cn: 交通配对：特快列车与快递都直达而迅速。

normal.en: The adjective with purpose means explicit, as in an express purpose.
normal.cn: 与「目的」一词连用的形容词义表示「明确的」，如明确目的。

normal.en: The family runs express, expression, expressive and expressly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括动词、名词、形容词与副词四种形式。

abstract.en: Picture an orange and a sentence both being squeezed by the same hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只橙子和一句话被同一只手挤压。

abstract.en: Picture a train that never stops until it reaches the coast.
abstract.cn: 想象一列火车一路不停，直到抵达海岸。

abstract.en: Picture a thought packed into a parcel and sent overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个想法被装进包裹，连夜寄出。

examples.en: She expressed her thanks with a small hand-written note.
examples.cn: 她用一张手写的小纸条表达了感谢。

examples.en: The factory expresses oil from locally grown seeds.
examples.cn: 这家工厂用当地种植的种子榨油。

examples.en: The express leaves the city at six and reaches the border by noon.
examples.cn: 特快列车六点离城，中午前到达边境。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「向外压」——把话压出来是说，把汁压出来是榨 → 表达、榨出

root: 拉丁语 exprimere「压出」= 表示「向外」的前缀 + premere「压」；premere 更深来源不确定，相关词根形式为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pressure: words out of a mind, feeling out through art, juice out of fruit, speed out of a schedule, clarity out of a statement, symbols out of a relation and a product out of a gene.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一股压力展开：从心里压出话语、通过艺术压出情感、从果子压出汁液、从时刻表压出速度、从陈述压出明确、从关系压出符号、从基因压出产物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand presses, and what was inside comes out.
core.cn: 核心意象：手一压，里面的东西就出来了。

branches.en: SAY AND SHOW: words and art are two outlets for the same inner pressure.
branches.cn: 说与显：词语与艺术是同一股内在压力的两个出口。

branches.en: LIQUID OUT: the literal squeeze that keeps the root meaning alive.
branches.cn: 汁液出来：字面上的挤压，让词根意义继续活着。

branches.en: DIRECT SPEED: a train and a parcel service both press straight through without delay.
branches.cn: 直达速度：列车与包裹服务都一路直推、不作耽搁。

branches.en: PRESSED INTO CLARITY: something expressly set out cannot be mistaken for an implication.
branches.cn: 压成清晰：特意摆出来的东西不会被误当成暗示。

branches.en: SYMBOL AND CELL: a formula and a gene both make an inner relation or instruction visible and active.
branches.cn: 符号与细胞：公式与基因都让内在关系或指令变得可见并发挥作用。

intro.en: Express is a Latin verb of pressing, and its parts also build nouns, adjectives and adverbs for showing and squeezing.
intro.cn: express 是一个表示「压」的拉丁动词，其部件还构成表示「表现」与「挤压」的名词、形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ex- 'out' and premere 'to press' form exprimere; the noun expressio and the adjective expressus extend the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「向外」的前缀与 premere「压」构成 exprimere；名词 expressio 与形容词 expressus 延续同一词族。

items.example: The prefix sends the action outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作送向外面。

items.example: The root names the force behind the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名动作背后的力量。

items.meaning: to press out; to say or show
items.example: The press expresses oil from the seeds.
items.exampleCN: 压榨机从种子里榨出油。

items.example: The letter was warm and expressive.
items.exampleCN: 这封信温暖而富有表现力。

items.example: The rules expressly forbid the practice.
items.exampleCN: 规则明确禁止这种做法。

items.structure: Italian espresso, from the same Latin verb
items.example: The barista pulled a short espresso.
items.exampleCN: 咖啡师压出一小杯浓缩咖啡。

items.meaning: to press a mark or feeling in
items.exampleCN: 这场演讲给听众留下了深刻印象。

scene: 她听到消息后没有说话，脸上的神情却先变了，同事低声说：Her expression changed before she found the words.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「脸上显示情绪的神情」（第 2 个义项：面部神情）；句意为她还没找到话说，神情就先变了。

表现主义
表现主义者；表现主义的

senses.title: The act of showing thoughts or feelings
senses.titleCN: 把想法或情感表达出来的行为
senses.definition: the act of making thoughts, feelings or ideas known
senses.definitionCN: 把想法、情感或观点让人知道的行为
senses.example: Freedom of expression is protected by law.
senses.exampleCN: 表达自由受法律保护。
senses.why: The core image is pressing something inward out into the open, and the first sense is simply that outward movement.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是把里面的东西压到外面来，第 1 个义项就是这一向外的动作本身。

senses.title: The look on a face
senses.definition: the appearance of a person's face that shows a feeling or state of mind
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的脸部外观所显示的情绪或心理状态
senses.example: His expression softened when he heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息，他的神情柔和下来。
senses.why: The face is the most visible surface where inner feeling is pressed into public view.
senses.whyCN: 脸是内心情感被压到公众视野里最显眼的表面。

senses.title: A word or phrase
senses.definition: a particular word, phrase or way of saying something
senses.definitionCN: 某个特定的词、短语或说法
senses.example: A local expression puzzled the translator.
senses.exampleCN: 一个当地说法让译者困惑。
senses.why: A fixed group of words is a small package into which a meaning has already been pressed.
senses.whyCN: 一组固定的词就像一个小包裹，意义早已被压进其中。

senses.title: Vivid delivery in speech or music
senses.titleCN: 说话或演奏时的表现力
senses.definition: the quality of conveying feeling through voice, phrasing or performance
senses.definitionCN: 通过嗓音、措辞或表演传达情感的特质
senses.example: She read the poem with great expression.
senses.exampleCN: 她极富表现力地朗读了这首诗。
senses.why: Once the outward push is done with skill, the delivery itself becomes noticeable and can be praised.
senses.whyCN: 当向外的推送带有技巧时，表达方式本身就会变得显眼并值得称赞。

senses.title: A mathematical expression
senses.definition: a combination of numbers, symbols and operations that stands for a value
senses.definitionCN: 由数字、符号与运算组成、代表某个值的组合
senses.example: Simplify the expression before substituting values.
senses.exampleCN: 先化简表达式，再代入数值。
senses.why: Mathematics writes a value as a visible string of symbols, pressing an abstract quantity into a readable form.
senses.whyCN: 数学把一个值写成可见的符号串，把抽象量压成可读的形式。

senses.title: Gene expression in biology
senses.definition: the process by which information in a gene is turned into a working product
senses.definitionCN: 基因中的信息被转成可用产物的过程
senses.example: The gene's expression rises under heat stress.
senses.exampleCN: 在热应激下，这个基因的表达增强。
senses.why: A gene carries hidden instructions, and expression is the moment those instructions are pushed out into the cell.
senses.whyCN: 基因携带隐藏的指令，表达就是这些指令被推到细胞里发挥作用的时刻。

senses.title: Pressing out juice or oil
senses.definition: the physical act of squeezing liquid out of fruit, seeds or peel
senses.definitionCN: 从果实、种子或果皮中挤出液体的物理动作
senses.example: Cold expression of the peel releases the essential oil.
senses.exampleCN: 冷榨果皮能释放出精油。
senses.why: This is the oldest concrete sense: the word's root literally means to press out, and liquids are pressed from plants.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的具体义：词根字面就是「压出来」，而液体正是从植物中被压出的。

senses.title: A manifestation or sign
senses.titleCN: 某种态度或品质的显现
senses.definition: an act or thing that shows a quality, attitude or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 显示某种品质、态度或情感的行为或事物
senses.example: The grant is an expression of confidence in the team.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔资助是对该团队信心的体现。
senses.why: The abstract sense generalizes the push: an inner attitude becomes visible through an outer act.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把「推送」一般化：内在态度通过外在行为变得可见。

intro.en: Expression comes through Old French from Latin expressio, a noun of action from exprimere 'to press out', built on ex- 'out' and premere 'to press'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: expression 经古法语来自拉丁语 expressio，这是动词 exprimere「压出」的行为名词，由拉丁语表示「向外」的前缀与 premere「压」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Premere meant 'to press'. Its deeper origin is not established, and the Indo-European root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: premere 意为「压」。其更深来源未得到证明，有人为它提出的印欧词根只是重构形式。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus premere produced exprimere 'to press out, squeeze out'; it also developed the sense 'to represent or portray'.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的拉丁前缀加 premere 构成 exprimere「压出、挤出」；它还发展出「表现、描绘」的意义。

items.en: The action noun expressio named both a physical pressing out and a representation in words or art.
items.cn: 行为名词 expressio 既指物理上的压出，也指用词语或艺术的表现。

items.en: Old French expression entered English in the fourteenth century, first as the act of expressing and as an utterance.
items.cn: 古法语 expression 在十四世纪进入英语，最初指表达的行为与说出的话。

items.en: The facial sense took shape in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, while algebra adopted the word for a symbolic string and biology adopted it for gene activity in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 面部义在十七至十八世纪成形；代数学采用这个词指符号串，生物学则在二十世纪用它指基因活动。

items.en: Source uncertain: the date of the facial sense is not exact, and the pre-Latin origin of premere remains unsettled, so every proposed root form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：面部义的确切年代不确定，premere 在拉丁语之前的来源也仍未确定，因此提出的各种词根形式都属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words built with the same pressing root but different prefixes; group two holds near neighbours in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「压」这一词根、但前缀不同的词；第二组是语义相近的词。

entries.definition: Built with 'in' rather than 'out': something presses into the mind and leaves an impression, not an outward expression.
entries.definitionCN: 用的是「向内」而非「向外」的前缀：某物压进心里留下印象，而不是向外的表达。

entries.definition: The prefix means 'together': it names pressing something into a smaller space, with no idea of showing meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀意为「共同」：指把某物压进更小的空间，与显示意义无关。

entries.definition: The prefix means 'under': it names holding something down or stopping it, often feelings or information.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀意为「在下」：指把某物压住或制止，常指情感或信息。

entries.definition: It looks as if it should belong to the pressing family, but its root means 'to appease or atone', not 'to press'.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像属于「压」这个词族，其实词根意为「安抚、赎罪」，并非「压」。

entries.definition: A plain word for the appearance of a face; expression adds the idea that the look reveals inner feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 指脸部外观的朴素词；expression 多了「神情显示内心情感」这一层。

entries.definition: A group of words forming a unit; expression can also mean a fixed saying, but it is broader and more idiomatic.
entries.definitionCN: 构成一个单位的词组；expression 也可指固定说法，但范围更宽、更习语化。

entries.definition: A technical term for a unit of speech; expression points more to the meaning being conveyed than to the sound produced.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个言语单位的技术术语；expression 更指向被传达的意义，而不是发出的声音。

entries.definition: A formal word for something that makes an inner quality visible, close to the eighth sense of expression.
entries.definitionCN: 指使内在品质变得可见的正式用词，接近 expression 的第 8 个义项。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the pressing root, the prefix contrasts and the real technical uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「压」的词根、前缀对比与真实的技术用法。

normal.en: The root means 'press', so expression is a pressing outward of what was inside.
normal.cn: 词根意为「压」，因此这个词就是把里面的东西向外压出来。

normal.en: Prefix contrast: outward pressing gives expression, inward pressing gives impression.
normal.cn: 前缀对比：向外压得到「表达」，向内压得到「印象」。

normal.en: Face use: the same word names the look that shows feeling.
normal.cn: 面部用法：同一个词也命名显示情感的神情。

normal.en: Technical spread: algebra uses it for a symbolic string, biology for gene activity.
normal.cn: 技术延伸：代数学用它指符号串，生物学用它指基因活动。

normal.en: Everyday phrase: freedom of expression names the right to make ideas public.
normal.cn: 日常搭配：表达自由指把想法公开的权利。

abstract.en: Picture a hand squeezing a fruit until the juice lands in a glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手挤压果子，汁水落进杯子里。

abstract.en: Picture an inner feeling rising to the surface of a face like water to a well.
abstract.cn: 想象内心的情感升到脸的表面，像水升到井口。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence folded into a small box that can be handed to someone.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话被折进一个小盒子，可以递给别人。

examples.en: The court treated the letter as an expression of intent.
examples.cn: 法院把这封信视为意向的表达。

examples.en: Her expression did not match the cheerful words she used.
examples.cn: 她的神情与她使用的欢快词语并不一致。

examples.en: The software evaluates each expression before running the program.
examples.cn: 软件在运行程序前先求值每一个表达式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「向外」加「压」——把心里的东西压出来 → 表达、表情

root: 拉丁语 exprimere「压出」= 表示「向外」的前缀 + premere「压」，其行为名词为 expressio；premere 更深来源不确定，相关印欧词根为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one outward push: the act itself, the face that shows it, the phrase that packages it, the delivery, the formula, the gene, the pressed juice and the visible sign.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次向外的推送展开：行为本身、显现在脸上、被包进词语、表现方式、公式、基因、榨出的汁液以及可见的迹象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something inside is pressed outward and becomes visible.
core.cn: 核心意象：里面的东西被向外压出，变得可见。

branches.en: OUTWARD ACT: making an inner state public and letting it appear as a sign are the same push seen at two levels.
branches.cn: 向外的行为：把内在状态公开，与让它显现为迹象，是同一个推送在两个层面上的样子。

branches.en: FACE: the most visible surface on which feeling is pressed into view.
branches.cn: 脸：情感被压到视野里最显眼的表面。

branches.en: PACKAGED WORDS: a fixed phrase is a small box that already holds a meaning.
branches.cn: 被包好的词语：一个固定短语就是一只已经装着意义的小盒子。

branches.en: FORCE AND DELIVERY: the pressure that squeezes oil also shapes the skilled delivery of a line.
branches.cn: 力量与表现：挤压油液的压力，也塑造一句台词的熟练表达。

branches.en: SYMBOLIC AND BIOLOGICAL EXPRESSION: a formula makes a value readable, and a gene makes its instructions active.
branches.cn: 符号与生物表达：公式让数值可读，基因让指令发挥作用。

intro.en: Expression is made of a Latin prefix, a Latin verb root and a noun suffix, and the same parts build a whole family of show-and-press words.
intro.cn: expression 由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁动词词根与一个名词后缀构成，同样的部件构成了一整族表示「压出与表现」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin premere 'to press' and ex- 'out' produce exprimere and its noun expressio; English adds the suffixes that build the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「压」的词根与表示「向外」的前缀构成 exprimere 及其名词 expressio；英语再加上构成词族的后缀。

items.example: The prefix directs the action away from the inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作引向外部。

items.example: The root supplies the physical force in the image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供意象中的物理力量。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a name for its action.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成其行为的名词。

items.example: The expression of grief took the form of silence.
items.exampleCN: 悲伤的表达采取了沉默的形式。

items.meaning: to press out; to say or show
items.example: He expressed his thanks in a short letter.
items.exampleCN: 他用一封短信表达了感谢。

items.example: Her expressive reading held the room.
items.exampleCN: 她富有表现力的朗读抓住了全场。

items.example: His expressionless face gave nothing away.
items.exampleCN: 他面无表情，没有泄露任何信息。

items.meaning: an art movement that distorts form to show feeling
items.meaningCN: 为表现情感而扭曲形式的艺术运动
items.example: Expressionism used violent colour to show inner states.
items.exampleCN: 表现主义用强烈的色彩显示内心状态。

items.example: The expressionist painted faces as blocks of colour.
items.exampleCN: 这位表现主义画家把脸画成色块。

definition_zh: 额外的；另外的；附加的（形容词）；额外的事物；临时演员（名词）；格外；特别（副词）
definition_en: more than what is usual or expected; added to the usual amount
core_image: 标准份之外的又一份：盘子边上多出来的那一小碟
scene: 旅店前台问要不要加床，爸爸看了看熟睡的孩子，点头说：We would like an extra blanket for the night.
sceneCN: 这里 extra 指「在标准之外另加的」（第 1 个义项：额外提供的）；句意为夜里需要再加一床毯子。

pos.zh: 额外的事物；另收费项目；临时演员

derivatives.zh: 非凡的；特别的（extra 加拉丁词根 ordinarius，义为「在常规秩序之外的」）
奢侈的；过度的（extra 加 vagari「游荡」，义为「游出边界之外的」）
外来的；无关的（同源正式词，义为「从外面进来的」）

senses.title: More than the usual amount
senses.definition: more of something than is usual, expected, or already provided
senses.definitionCN: 超出通常、预期或既定供给的量
senses.example: We would like an extra blanket for the night.
senses.exampleCN: 我们想夜里再加一床毯子。
senses.why: The Latin root means beyond or outside: the extra thing stands at the edge of the standard plate.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根义为「在…之外」：extra 的东西就站在标准盘子的边缘。

senses.title: Additional payment or charge
senses.definition: money charged beyond the normal price
senses.definitionCN: 超出正常价格的收费
senses.example: Breakfast at the hotel costs extra.
senses.exampleCN: 旅馆的早餐要另外收费。
senses.why: The beyond-position turns to money: outside the fixed bill, one more sum waits.
senses.whyCN: 「之外」的位置换成了钱：固定账单之外还有一笔在等着。

senses.title: A person with no speaking part
senses.definition: a film or theatre performer without a speaking role
senses.definitionCN: 电影或戏剧中没有台词的表演者
senses.example: Hundreds of extras filled the battle scene.
senses.exampleCN: 数百名临时演员填满了战争场面。
senses.why: A person added beyond the needed cast: outside the story's main count, but visible on screen.
senses.whyCN: 超出必要班底而加上的人：不在主角计数之内，却在镜头里。

senses.title: Especially; very
senses.definition: used before an adjective to mean very or unusually
senses.definitionCN: 用在形容词前表示「非常」「格外」
senses.example: Be extra careful on the icy road.
senses.exampleCN: 结冰的路上要格外小心。
senses.why: The beyond-image intensifies: past the usual degree, one more step out.
senses.whyCN: 「之外」的意象转为强调：越过寻常程度，再往外一步。

intro.en: Extra is a Latin adverb meaning "beyond, outside", taken straight into English and grown into an adjective.
intro.cn: extra 是拉丁语副词「在…之外」，直接进入英语并长成形容词。

items.en: Latin extra meant "outside, beyond", used in phrases like extra muros, outside the walls.
items.cn: 拉丁语 extra 意为「在外面、超出」，用于 extra muros（城墙之外）等短语。

items.en: It is a cousin of exterus, "outward", which gave English external and exterior.
items.cn: 它是 exterus「向外的」的近亲，后者衍生出英语 external 与 exterior。

items.en: Eighteenth-century English borrowed it as an adjective, "added beyond the ordinary".
items.cn: 十八世纪英语把它借作形容词，义为「超出寻常之外而另加的」。

items.en: The noun followed in commerce: extras were items billed beyond the base price.
items.cn: 名词随之进入商业语：extras 指基本价之外的另计项目。

items.en: The adverb use as an intensifier and the film-extra sense completed the family.
items.cn: 作强调副词的用法与「临时演员」义补齐了这个词族。

note.en: These neighbours carry the same outside-the-line prefix or a related idea.
note.cn: 下列词带同样的「越界」前缀，或意思相近。

entries.definition: far beyond the ordinary
entries.definitionCN: 非凡的（extra + ordinary，常规之外）

entries.definition: spending beyond all limits
entries.definitionCN: 奢侈的（同前缀，游出边界）

entries.definition: on the outside
entries.definitionCN: 外部的（同 exterus 词根）

entries.definition: to draw out
entries.definitionCN: 提取；拔出（同前缀 ex-，义为「拉出来」）

entries.definition: added on
entries.definitionCN: 另外的；附加的（中性书面）

entries.definition: kept in reserve
entries.definitionCN: 备用的；多余的

entries.definition: amount left over beyond need
entries.definitionCN: 盈余；过剩（偏数量结果）

normalIntro.en: Five associations from the real root and usage.
normalIntro.cn: 五条来自真实词根与用法的联想。

normal.en: Extra in Latin simply means outside or beyond.
normal.cn: extra 在拉丁语里就是「外面、超出」。

normal.en: Extraordinary is the family star: beyond the ordinary.
normal.cn: extraordinary 是词族明星：超出寻常。

normal.en: Costs extra is the shop phrase for beyond the base price.
normal.cn: costs extra 是商店用语：基本价之外另算。

normal.en: Film extras are people added beyond the needed cast.
normal.cn: 电影里的 extra 是超出必要班底加上去的人。

normal.en: Extra large pushes size one step past large.
normal.cn: extra large 把尺码在 large 之上再推一步。

abstract.en: Picture a dinner plate: beside the standard serving sits one more small dish.
abstract.cn: 想象餐盘：标准份旁边又多了一小碟。

abstract.en: The edge of the standard is where everything extra lives.
abstract.cn: 所有 extra 都住在标准线的边缘。

abstract.en: Going beyond can be generous, costly, or simply off the wall.
abstract.cn: 「越出一步」可以是慷慨、昂贵，也可以是离谱。

examples.en: We would like an extra blanket for the night.
examples.cn: 我们想夜里再加一床毯子。

examples.en: Breakfast at the hotel costs extra.
examples.cn: 旅馆的早餐要另外收费。

examples.en: Be extra careful on the icy road.
examples.cn: 结冰的路上要格外小心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱克斯戳」——爱克斯（X）之外再戳一份，就是额外的。

root: 拉丁语副词 extra「在外面、超出」，与 exterus「向外的」（external、exterior）同族。十八世纪进入英语作形容词，随后派生名词、副词与「临时演员」义。

sensesIntro.en: From standing outside the standard, the word covers added amounts, added bills, added people, and added intensity.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「站在标准之外」出发，覆盖另加的量、另收的费、另加的人与格外强调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one more dish set at the edge of the standard plate
core.cn: 核心意象：标准盘边多出的一小碟

branches.en: beyond the usual measure or degree
branches.cn: 超出寻常的量或程度

branches.en: beyond the fixed bill
branches.cn: 固定账单之外的部分

branches.en: people beyond the needed cast
branches.cn: 必要班底之外的人

branches.en: added items share the outside position
branches.cn: 另加项同处「之外」位置

branches.en: the added ones stand at the frame's edge
branches.cn: 另加者站在画面边缘

intro.en: The family lives on the Latin ex- outside-line, stacking with other roots.
intro.cn: 词族生在拉丁 ex- 的「界外」义上，可与其他词根叠加。

latinIntro.en: Latin cousins keeping the beyond sense.
latinIntro.cn: 保留「超出」义的拉丁同族词。
